dunia-innovations-berlin::2516220.title: Head of AI Research
dunia-innovations-berlin::2516220.desc: Define how AI can understand, reason about, and discover materials Dunia is building AI for one of the hardest unsolved problems in science: turning materials discovery from an academic, trial-and-error process into a programmable, scalable discipline. As Head of AI Research, you will define and lead Dunia’s AI-for-Materials agenda at the intersection of machine learning, physics, chemistry, and automated experimentation. This role is about more than applying existing ML techniques to scientific data. It is about inventing the representations, learning paradigms, and evaluation frameworks that allow AI to reason about matter across scales. You will spearhead the development of Dunia's Materials World Model, shaping how AI interacts with experiments and simulations, and how scientific insight is translated into systems that reliably produce new materials with real-world impact. Your tasks will include: Set the intellectual direction for AI for Materials Define Dunia’s research thesis for AI-native materials discovery Identify where existing ML paradigms fail when applied to physical matter, and what must be built instead Decide which research bets have the potential to shift the field, not just improve benchmarks Build and lead a world-class research team Hire, mentor, and challenge senior ML researchers and scientists Create an environment that values deep thinking, honest evaluation, and intellectual courage Set a high bar for scientific taste, clarity, and originality Turn research into systems that discover Work closely with Programs, Hardware & Automation, and Software Architecture to embed research into end-to-end discovery loops Ensure models are grounded in physical reality and experimental feedback, not just data abstractions Balance long-horizon research with near-term delivery without reducing ambition Shape the external field Influence how AI for Materials is discussed, evaluated, and pursued across academia and industry Build collaborations that extend Dunia’s reach while protecting focus and IP Represent a clear, opinionated point of view on where the field should go next PhD in ML; background in physics, chemistry, or a related field desired 7 + year's experience in AI research, including leadership of senior ICs Deep experience in representation learning, scientific ML, or foundation models Strong intuition for physical systems and their constraints Proven ability to operate at the boundary between theory, systems, and real-world feedback High scientific taste and comfort making irreversible prioritization decisions under uncertainty Clear communicator who can align researchers, engineers, and leadership around ambitious goals English fluency, additional languages preferred

dunia-innovations-berlin::2516249.title: Materials Informatics Scientist (Evaluation-focused)
dunia-innovations-berlin::2516249.desc: Define how AI models for materials discovery are evaluated, compared, and trusted Dunia is building AI for one of the hardest unsolved problems in science: turning materials discovery from an academic, trial-and-error process into a programmable, scalable discipline. As our models grow more complex and our experimental throughput increases, the limiting factor is no longer generating predictions, but knowing which ones to believe. As Materials Informatics Scientist (Evaluation-focused), you will own the evaluation and validation of AI models applied to materials discovery. Your role is to ensure that model performance claims are meaningful, comparable, and decision-relevant, and that progress in AI for Materials reflects real improvements in discovery, not artifacts of metrics or datasets. This role is not about building new models. It is about defining the standards by which models are judged. Your tasks will include: Own evaluation as a scientific discipline Design, implement, and maintain evaluation frameworks for AI models across materials discovery tasks Define metrics and protocols that reflect generalization, robustness, uncertainty, and experimental relevance Identify failure modes, dataset leakage, and misleading performance signals Interrogate and compare models Systematically benchmark different model classes, training regimes, and representations Evaluate tradeoffs between accuracy, uncertainty, data efficiency, and usability Provide clear, defensible recommendations on which models to trust, deploy, or retire Connect AI performance to real outcomes Link model behavior to experimental results and program-level objectives Distinguish improvements that change decisions from those that only improve abstract scores Help research and programs teams understand what current models can and cannot reliably do Build robust analytical tooling Develop and maintain professional-grade scripts and analysis pipelines for evaluation and benchmarking Visualize complex, high-dimensional results in ways that surface real insight Ensure disciplined, reproducible handling of data, code, and results Communicate truth clearly Present findings clearly to AI researchers, materials scientists, and leadership Produce concise summaries that align the organization around a shared view of evidence and uncertainty Act as an independent scientific reference point when claims require validation PhD (strongly preferred) or Master’s degree in materials science, chemistry, physics, machine learning, or a related field Significant experien ce (typically 5–8 years ) working with scientific or ML systems under real-world uncertainty Demonstrated experience evaluating, benchmarking, or validating models rather than only building them Strong programming skills in Python and scientific data tooling Deep appreciation for rigor, reproducibility, and careful interpretation of results English fluency, additional languages preferred

TSMC Arizona - Yield Excellence Engineer
esmc-dresden::careers.tsmc.com/en_us/car.desc: TSMC Arizona - Yield Excellence Engineer TSMC Arizona - Yield Excellence Engineer Company TSMC Arizona Corporation Location USA-Arizona Career Area Manufacturing (fabs) Job Type Engineer / Admin Employment Type Regular Posted Oct 30, 2026 A job at TSMC Arizona offers an opportunity to work at one of the most advanced semiconductor fabs in the United States. Today, TSMC Arizona’s first fab is in full operations on its N5 and N4 process technology. Its second fab will utilize its N3 process technology and will start operations in the second half of 2027. It’s third fab will manufacture chips using 2nm or even more advanced process technology, with production starting by the end of the decade. America’s leading technology companies rely on TSMC Arizona for the next generations of chips that will power the AI and digital future. A job at TSMC Arizona offers an opportunity to work at the most advanced semiconductor fab in the United States. TSMC Arizona’s first fab will operate it’s leading-edge semiconductor process technology (N4 process), starting production in the first half of 2025. The second fab will utilize its leading edge N3 and N2 process technology and be operational in 2028. The recently announced third fab will manufacture chips using 2nm or even more advanced process technology, with production starting by the end of the decade. America’s leading technology companies are ready to rely on TSMC Arizona for the next generations of chips that will power the digital future. Shaping change: that is what drives us at Forschungszentrum Jülich. As a member of the Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft, our 7,700 employees conduct interdisciplinary research into the digitalized society, a climate-friendly energy system, and sustainable management. We focus our research on the natural sciences, life sciences, and engineering on the fields of information, energy, and bioeconomy. We combine this with expertise in high-performance computing and artificial intelligence, using unique scientific infrastructures. At Forschungszentrum Jülich, Research Software Engineering is understood as an integral part of modern research work. Our developers design, program, and operate software solutions that enable scientific breakthroughs in a wide range of disciplines - from energy and climate research to life sciences, materials science, and information technology. The spectrum ranges from the design of user-oriented web platforms to the development of highly optimized codes for supercomputers and quantum computers. Get to know JuRSE, the community of practice for scientists who code Working areas In the field of Research Software Engineering at Forschungszentrum Jülich, you will be working on the following areas: High-performance computing & research software Development, optimization, and maintenance of scientific software for current and future high-performance computers, including exascale systems, GPU-accelerated platforms, and RISC-V architectures. Data analysis, AI, and cloud platforms Development and expansion of platforms and tools for the management, processing, and analysis of large amounts of scientific data - from cloud services and IoT integration to applications in the field of artificial intelligence. Quantum and hybrid systems Supporting research through software solutions that enable access to novel quantum computers, their integration into hybrid supercomputer environments, and the development of interfaces and algorithms. Visualization & virtual reality Development of applications that visualize complex simulations and data in real time - for example, through virtual reality technologies that offer researchers new insights and opportunities for interaction. We are aware that women often face particular challenges in their professional lives - whether due to unconscious bias, the compatibility of career and care work or structural barriers. We therefore take targeted measures to actively promote equal opportunities in the application process. Facts and figures Statistics on applications from 2024 show that although only 34 % of applications were from women, women made up 54 % of those applicants who were invited to interviews. Women also make up a disproportionately high share of new recruits, accounting for 41% of new employees. These figures show how women are not discriminated against in our application process. On the contrary, as a woman, you have a good chance of being invited to interview and ultimately being recruited at Forschungszentrum Jülich. Gender equality and gender diversity are integral parts of Forschungszentrum Jülich’s values and objectives. The Gender Equality Plan contains further information on the measures taken in the area of recruitment and on achieving gender balance in leadership positions. Job advertisements Job requirements : Studies show that women are more likely to apply for a job only if they meet almost all of the requirements. This is why we would particularly encourage women applicants to apply for a position if the job description appeals to them, even if they do not meet 100 % of the requirements. Wording : Our gender-neutral job advertisements are reviewed and revised by our recruiting team before publication to ensure that the wording used is appropriate and appeals to women in particular. Diversity statement : “We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us.” You will find this diversity statement in all our job advertisements – we aim to continuously promote diversity among our employees! Selection process Overview of the application process The selection process may include a short video interview as part of a pre-selection round and will always consist of an in-depth interview (virtual or on site). Interviews at Forschungszentrum Jülich are conducted on an equal footing and are intended to help both sides reach a decision. fz-juelich-self-driving-labs::www.fz-jue.desc: Queer in Science 2025 Skip to main content Skip to navigation Skip to footer Press Sitemap Intranet de en / Careers / Working at Forschungszentrum Jülich / Career events / Queer in Science 2025 Queer in Science 2025 On September 2, 2025, we held our online event “Queer in Science” – it was an inspiring morning full of exchange, perspectives, and moments of encouragement. In an open panel discussion, four queer colleagues from science and science management shared their personal experiences. Topics: The importance of role models and networks for visibility and support Dealing with experiences of discrimination and helpful coping strategies Concrete measures that research institutions can take to create an inclusive and safe working environment The importance of visible role models , strong networks , and an open culture of support was emphasized. Visibility and solidarity are crucial for everyone to reach their potential. Our participants also contributed valuable perspectives through surveys, comments, and the chat. The discussion was impressively captured in a graphic recording that visually summarizes the central ideas and messages—a creative reflection of this enriching exchange. If you are interested in a visiting program or online event with queer role models, please contact us. For a visit, it is ideal if the group size is at least 15 people. globalfoundries-dresden::JR-2606508.desc: About GF GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors that enable AI at scale, from the cloud to the physical world. We partner closely with our customers to deliver differentiated, power-efficient, high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. Across our global footprint in the United States, Europe and Asia, our teams are solving complex challenges that shape the future of technology. At GF, you'll find the opportunity to make an impact, work with world-class talent and contribute to a more secure, sustainable future. Your Job In semiconductor manufacturing, no processing machine runs continuously yielding the same results. Materials used in the machine can degrade over time, simple factors like –outside temperature can fluctuate, and high usage and low usage play a roll. For stable process results, specific machine settings and recipe parameters are tuned automatically or manually. This is an essential part of work for our process and equipment experts. As a PhD candidate, you will be looking differently at our machines and processes. You already have a scientist´s or an engineer´s view. You know and see the parameters available, regardless of current usage. There, your journey starts towards finding the optimal machine and process settings with as few as possible latest data points. Latest advances in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence indicate the possibility for improvements and will guide your research. The goal of this work shall be the summary and testing of state-of-the-art methods in real-world applications as well as development of new methods tailored to the needs of the semiconductor industry, so in this work Data Science approaches are to be developed to enable process experts to use ML and AI for machine and process tuning. The contract for this position is set up for 3 years with the possibility to extend it by one additional year, if required. We are looking for a research associate who wants to take a coordinating role in a joint project with other partners from academia and industry and in aligning their research work to the requirements of later mass production. You will systematically document and present the results in regular reports. GF supports the publication of scientific results in leading journals and the protection of intellectual property by the submission of patents. icn2-bellaterra::jobs.icn2.cat/job-openi.desc: Junior Group Leader in the field of Quantum Optoelectronics | Job openings and fellowships | ICN2 - Institut Català de Nanociència i Nanotecnologia Back Process in the Interviews phase Download PDF About ICN2 As a flagship research centre in nanoscience and nanotechnology, ICN2 mission is to open and explore new frontiers of knowledge at the nanoscale and bring value to society in the form of new understanding, capabilities and innovation, while inspiring and providing broad training to the next generations of researchers. Our values are Commitment, Collaboration and Transformation. Our research lines focus on the newly discovered physical and chemical properties that arise from the behaviour of matter at the nanoscale. ICN2 has been awarded with the Severo Ochoa Centre of Excellence distinction for three consecutive periods (2014-2018 and 2018-2022 and 2023-2026). ICN2 comprises 20 Research Groups, 7 Technical Development and Support Units and Facilities, and 2 Research Platforms, covering different areas of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Quantum Initiatives at ICN2: ICN2 is actively involved in national quantum initiatives, including the Quantum Communication National Plan, as well as regional efforts such as the Quantum Catalan Academy ( https://cataloniaquantum.eu/ ) and the Master in Quantum Science and Technology ( https://quantummasterbarcelona.eu/ ). These initiatives contribute to a dynamic ecosystem that fosters talent attraction and retention while supporting the development of new research lines. Our recently established Quantum Synergy Laboratory further reinforces our commitment to pioneering advancements in quantum science. Job Title: Junior Group Leader in the field of Quantum Optoelectronics Description : We are seeking a Junior Research Group Leader with an outstanding record in nanoscience and nanotechnology. imec-leuven::www.imec-int.com/en/work-at.title: Liquid AI Business Models Rethink the economics of AI compute as it flows from the cloud to the edge
imec-leuven::www.imec-int.com/en/work-at.desc: Liquid AI Business Models | imec / Liquid AI Business Models Liquid AI Business Models PhD - Gent | Just now Rethink the economics of AI compute as it flows from the cloud to the edge Apply This PhD aims to study techno-economic and business impact of distributed AI compute. AI is the most disruptive technology in the domains covered by HIPEAC in the last decades. Apart from boosting chip development companies like NVIDIA to extreme valuations, it made model developers like OpenAi and Anthropic investing massively in AI data centers, trying to stay ahead of the competition. This led to a range of issues in terms of energy consumption, availably of components, reliability, etc. As an alternative to the systematic request for cloud services, Europe (HiPEAC report) suggests the Next Computing Paradigm (NCP) based on distributed computing on demand, where AI compute shifts from big, centralized data centers towards more distributed "liquid" setups, running on edge devices, on-premise, or even orchestrated across many owners' devices. In the light of this expected shift, the central research question of this PhD is “ Which business models make the shift towards liquid AI economically viable?” As this overarching question should tackled from different angles, the following three sub-questions will be studied. (1) W hat drives the cost of the different AI architectures? This question takes the perspective of the AI provider and aims to understand their cost model. It investigates how the costs of AI compare across the spectrum: central cloud vs. edge vs. liquid, big and general-purpose LLMs versus small, task-specialized SAM (small and specialized models). It takes into account the moving importance from training to inference and consider investment as well as operational costs. (2) What are viable revenue models for AI usage? This question takes the perspective of the AI user and compares the current default of token base pricing to subscription, infrastructure/utility, hardware-as-a-service, compute-sharing marketplaces. What is the impact of the different pricing models on the business model for the AI users? How does it impact AI driven companies' strategic choices like cloud versus self-hosted AI solutions? (3) What is the impact on the business models for different actors across AI stack? How does value creation and value capture shift along the value chain (model providers, chip/device makers, hyper-scalers, orchestration layers)? Which models are economically viable for the AI providers (trade-off between costs and revenues) so that we get to an economically viable solution when token subsidization stops? This PhD will develop a novel techno-economic methodology that combines bottom-up cost modeling and multi-actor value-network analysis. The liquid compute exchange is modelled as a two-sided market and the orchestrator can be a distinct value-capture layer. A suitable PhD candidate combines expertise from both technical and economic perspective

lam-research-fremont-usa::206650.desc: The group you’ll be a part of In the Global Products Group, we are dedicated to excellence in the design and engineering of Lam's etch and deposition products. We drive innovation to ensure our cutting-edge solutions are helping to solve the biggest challenges in the semiconductor industry. The impact you’ll make As a Process Engineer at Lam, you will operate on cutting-edge technology, harnessing atomic precision, material science, and surface engineering to push technical boundaries. Your role involves developing new and advanced process formulations, defining equipment hardware to meet processing requirements, evaluating test data, and coordinating design requirements to ensure compatibility of processing methods. Your expertise and knowledge play a crucial role our customers success, making an impact on the next generation of semiconductor breakthroughs. What you’ll do Conduct process engineering research, development, and evaluation in support of Lam’s cutting- edge semiconductor equipment and systems. Review and enhance processing techniques and methods applied in the manufacture and fabrication of products. Develop and sustain new processes and process improvements to reduce production costs and increase yields. Compile and analyze test data to establish next steps in process development and determine appropriate limits and variables for process specifications. Collaborate internally to plan, collect data, analyze results, and report on customer demos for existing process applications. Partner cross-functionally and with customers to understand roadmaps, process flow, inflection points, requirements, and business challenges. Contribute to next generation product development and release activities supporting the semiconductor roadmap. Provide leadership, clear direction, and guidance to process technicians to support execution activities. Who we’re looking for Master’s degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry or Physics or related field with 10+ years of experience; or a PhD with 6+ years’ experience; or a Bachelor’s degree with 15+ years of experience in related field. Preferred qualifications Familiarity with working in a laboratory and on semiconductor equipment with experience in surface preparation and analytical techniques. More than 5 years of relevant work experience with wet-clean and spin-clean semiconductor industry processes. Strong organizational skills and demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. Ability to react to shifting priorities to meet business needs and deadlines. In-depth understanding of Statistical Process Control (SPC) and/or Design of Experiments (DOE). Working knowledge of statistical analysis and problem-solving methodologies. lam-research-fremont-usa::205800.desc: About the role: Lam Research is seeking a highly motivated Process Engineer 3 (PE3) to join the Global Metrology Team. The engineer will lead the application of in-situ diagnostic techniques including GP-FTIR, FTIR, Mass Spectrometry (MS), UV-Vis, Raman spectroscopy, and related technologies to establish mechanistic understanding of complex process interactions and enable next-generation process control strategies. Responsibilities include developing predictive metrology frameworks and calibrated defectivity models to support process optimization, simulation activities, and advanced defect monitoring. This role will collaborate closely with process, product, defect inspection, and simulation teams to advance Lam’s metrology and defectivity roadmap. The engineer will evaluate and deploy emerging inspection and review technologies, including next-generation e-beam platforms, to enable high-sensitivity defect detection and predictive inspection capabilities for complex semiconductor manufacturing applications. As a member of the Global Metrology Team, the successful candidate will recommend and implement innovative metrology solutions that strengthen Lam’s technical leadership, enhance product competitiveness, and support future technology development initiatives. The role will also be responsible for establishing and executing SPC-based monitoring and qualification methodologies to ensure critical metrology assets operate at optimal performance and meet long-term capability and reliability objectives. lam-research-fremont-usa::204453.title: Senior Computational Scientist / Software Engineer - Feature Scale Process Simulation
lam-research-fremont-usa::204453.desc: About the Role We are seeking an experienced Computational Software Engineer to help develop the next generation of physics-based semiconductor process simulation technologies. This position is based in Lam Research's Greater Boston area engineering office, where you will work alongside software developers, computational scientists, and semiconductor process experts developing advanced modeling solutions for next-generation semiconductor manufacturing. This role focuses on the development of advanced feature-scale simulation software that predicts the evolution of nanoscale semiconductor structures during plasma etch, deposition, and other manufacturing processes. You will work at the intersection of software engineering, computational physics, and semiconductor process technology. The successful candidate will contribute both to the scientific modeling of plasma-surface interactions and to the design and implementation of high-performance simulation software used by researchers, process engineers, and product development teams. This position requires a unique combination of strong software development skills and a deep understanding of the physical processes that drive feature evolution during semiconductor manufacturing. Responsibilities • Design, implement, and maintain computational software for feature-scale semiconductor process simulation. • Develop and enhance physics-based models describing plasma-surface interactions, surface chemistry, material transport, and profile evolution. • Translate physical theories, experimental observations, and mathematical models into robust, production-quality software. • Collaborate with plasma physicists, process engineers, computational scientists, and product teams to improve model fidelity and predictive capability. • Develop numerical algorithms for geometry evolution, particle transport, surface reaction kinetics, and related multiphysics phenomena. • Optimize simulation performance for modern computing architectures, including multicore CPUs and GPU-based systems. • Validate model predictions against experimental and metrology data. • Contribute to software architecture, testing frameworks, code reviews, and engineering best practices. • Investigate emerging approaches including machine learning, surrogate modeling, and digital twin technologies to accelerate simulation workflows. • Publish technical results and contribute to patents, conference presentations, and scientific publications when appropriate. Required Qualifications Ph.D. or M.S. in Physics, Computational Science, Applied Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Computer Science, or related technical discipline. Familiarity developing feature-scale, topography, or process simulation tools for plasma etch and deposition Strong software development experience in C++ and Python Experience developing numerical simulation or scientific computing software. We are currently looking for an energetic Material Scientist – pure silicon anode to join our innovative and ambitious organization. About LeydenJar At LeydenJar Technologies , we’re on a mission to redefine the future of energy storage. Our goal is to become the world’s innovation leader in advanced battery anodes, empowering the next generation of batteries that drive progress. Why does this matter? Because the world needs higher energy density batteries not just for better consumer electronics, but for electric vehicles, e-flight, and beyond. While the battery industry typically advances by only 3% per year, our breakthrough pure silicon anode technology delivers an improvement of up to 70%, a true game changer. Often called the “holy grail” of the battery industry, our technology unlocks new possibilities for electrification, sustainability, and resilience in global supply chains. What we do: · We produce pure silicon anode rolls that fit seamlessly into existing battery cell manufacturing lines, enabling customers to make a quantum leap in performance or create entirely new product categories. · Our initial focus is on consumer electronics, with automotive applications already in development. · By leveraging semiconductor thin-film technology (plasma deposition) and scaling it to battery anodes, we’ve overcome the long-standing challenges of silicon in batteries, delivering durability and efficiency at scale. To meet global demand, we’re scaling up: · PlantOne in Eindhoven opened in 2026 and is now ramping up to produce anode rolls and validate our roll-to-roll production tools. · PlantTwo , our large-scale production facility, will follow, establishing LeydenJar as a key player in the global battery market. This is an enormous opportunity and an ambitious journey. It requires bold, creative, and diverse minds who share our passion for innovation and sustainability. At LeydenJar, we value different perspectives, inclusive collaboration, and gender equality because we know that diversity fuels breakthrough ideas. Your mission As a Material Scientist in Product Development Department, you play a key role in designing, synthesizing, characterizing and optimizing pure silicon anodes, and you take end-to-end ownership of the development topics that turn our technology into products. You own your topics from hypothesis to validated result: you design and run the experimental work, characterize the material, conduct the in-depth analysis, and drive the technical decision that follows. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next. Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search. As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns. lila-sciences-us::4477308009.desc: Your Impact at LILA Lila runs autonomous science facilities — labs full of instruments, robotics, and controllers that produce the experimental data that is the company's core IP. The role sits at the seam between IT, Lab IT, and OT, spanning four workstreams: OT asset visibility and tooling, vulnerability and patch management across IT/OT, SOC integration and threat intelligence, and program build. The work product outlives the term. lila-sciences-us::4467398009.desc: Your Impact at LILA As a Co-Op on the Production Robotics team at Lila Sciences, you will help build the algorithms and software that let our robots know where they are and what they are looking at, so they can run scientific workflows reliably inside the AI Science Factories (AISFs). The output is software that runs in production lab environments and directly accelerates the rate at which Lila can run experiments. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end. lila-sciences-us::4395725009.desc: Your Impact at LILA Lila is redefining the future of medicine by combining automated large-scale data generation with scientific superintelligence. At Lila, we are building the loop where AI, automation, and experimental biology co-evolve to solve the hardest problems in medicine. The Life Science AI team develops machine learning systems for automated reasoning on biological data, combining state-of-the-art ML with breakthrough biology. We seek a Senior ML Scientist to focus on domain models underneath that system: models of perturbation biology, genetics, and and high-dimensional experimental readouts that connect biological mechanism, experimental intervention and therapeutic opportunity. At Lila, the data is generated for the model: we run our own experiments at scale, and you will help decide what gets measured. The question is not only what to learn from a fixed dataset, but what datasets should exist. And model outputs are reasoned over. Predictions go to systems and scientists choosing what to run next and making mechanistic calls downstream. Both need to know why, not only what. A model that returns a quantity a biologist, human or AI, can argue with; models that transfer to new contexts, compose into a downstream calculation, and can be checked against an independent measurement are often worth more than a more accurate one that returns an embedding. What You'll Be Building Build domain models for perturbation, genetic, and multimodal experimental data, and translate biological questions into rigorous ML problem formulations. Where the biology supports it, build models with interpretable structure — representations grounded in the machinery that executes a biological process rather than in cell-type identity embeddings, and parameters a biologist can argue with. Make uncertainty a deliverable. Calibrated posteriors, honest error bars, and outputs that tell a downstream consumer how much a prediction can actually settle — particularly when predicting into conditions never measured. Pre-register and beat baselines. Simple entity-mean, additive, and linear baselines are stated before any model is fit. If the full model does not beat them, we ship the baseline and say so. Partner with experimental scientists to guide data generation and model validation — shaping what gets measured, in what contexts, at what precision — and build the experiment-selection methods that choose the next batch of measurements to reduce uncertainty where it matters. Design benchmarks that connect model performance to biological and therapeutic consequence, apply model outputs to prioritize targets and mechanisms, and contribute technical direction to high-impact modeling programs. Support the integration of domain models into agentic workflows. Deploy tools, help engineer the agent harnesses that incorporate these tools and collaborate on creating environments to train the reasoning models that drive these agents. We are seeking a Senior ML Scientist to connect that work to human medicine, building the systems that assess whether a clinical program's biology holds up. Three questions define the work. Is the mechanism well supported? What has actually been established about how this intervention is meant to work, and what has only been assumed. Does the mechanism operate in patients? Human genetics, expression, cohort and prior-trial evidence all bear on whether the biology that works in a model system is present, and rate-limiting, in the population being treated. Is the trial built for that mechanism? Endpoints that read out the right thing on the right timescale, biomarkers that measure what the mechanism actually does, and enrollment criteria that select patients in whom it is operative — or, very often, none of these. You will not answer these program by program yourself. You will build the systems that do it, drawing on the mechanistic models and structured biological evidence the rest of the group generates, and grounding them in human data. Your own judgment is the specification and the standard those systems are held to, and you will build the evaluations — including forecasts of real program outcomes scored against what was knowable at the time — that tell you whether they are any good. What You'll Be Building Build systems that assess mechanistic support for a clinical program. Take the structured biological evidence and mechanistic models generated elsewhere in the group and turn them into an assessment of whether an intervention's proposed mechanism is established, assumed, or unexamined. Ground mechanism in human data. Analyze human genetic, expression, cohort and trial-derived evidence to determine whether a mechanism is present, active and rate-limiting in the relevant patient population — and how heterogeneous it is across that population. Assess trial design against mechanism. Evaluate endpoint choice and timing, biomarker definition and assay, dose and schedule, and eligibility and enrichment criteria for alignment with the proposed mechanism, and encode that assessment so it can be applied at scale rather than case by case. Build the evaluations that hold these systems to account, including outcome-verifiable forecasts of real program progression scored using only information available at the prediction date, with the evidence boundary enforced against contamination. Run them yourself and report honestly when a contribution adds nothing. Co-design with ML scientists, mechanism scientists and engineers, translate model output into decisions people actually make, and publish — what is and is not predictable from mechanistic and human evidence is a real scientific question we intend to answer in public. michelin-clermont-ferrand::R-2026038884.desc: Trainee - - - - - - - - - - - - 📍 Localisation : Michelin Innovation Park - Cataroux, à Clermont-Ferrand - France 🎓 Niveau d'études : Bac +5 📅 Date de début : A partir de Janvier 2027 ⏱️ Durée: 5 à 6 mois Contexte : Durant les prochaines décennies, l’évolution des technologies informatiques et des télécommunications transformera la mobilité : véhicules semi-autonomes ou autonomes, mobilité connectée et usages prédictifs de maintenance deviennent des enjeux centraux. Dans ce cadre, la compréhension et le suivi de l’évolution des propriétés des pneumatiques tout au long de leur vie est un élément clé pour assurer sécurité, performance et planification d’opérations de maintenance. Les approches combinant modèles physiques et méthodes « data-driven » issues des statistiques et du Machine Learning constituent un domaine majeur de recherche et d’ingénierie. Le concept de Tire Digital Twin (Jumeau Numérique du Pneu), en complément de la mobilité connectée, offre un cadre pertinent pour développer des capacités prédictives et des outils d’aide à la décision basés sur des données temporelles et des modèles hybrides. Mission : Le stage permettra au/à la stagiaire de travailler sur l’intégration et l’évaluation de méthodes d’analyse et de modélisation de données liées aux pneumatiques et à leur usage. L’objectif est d’améliorer la robustesse et la qualité des estimations et prédictions à partir de signaux et séries temporelles, en s’appuyant sur des méthodes statistiques avancées et des techniques d’apprentissage automatique. Principales activités : · Data science · Analyses statistiques poussées · Séries temporelles · Création et évaluation de modèles · Augmentation de la robustesse des estimations et des prédictions · Machine Learning / Deep Learning · Approches d’hybridation entre modèles physiques et modèles « data-driven » · Visualisation et communication des résultats · Prétraitement et nettoyage de données Le/la stagiaire pourra : réaliser une revue bibliographique sur les méthodes pertinentes à utiliser, concevoir et implémenter des prototypes de modèles (ou pipelines) combinant approches physiques et approches « data-driven », et tester leur performance et leur robustesse sur des jeux de données disponibles. Délivrables : Les attendus en fin de stage sont : - Un rapport présentant les différents travaux réalisés - Un apport aux boites à outils utilisées dans l’équipe. Apports pour le candidat : - Etre intégré à une équipe multi-disciplinaire d’ingénieurs, docteurs et docteurs-ingénieurs, développant des services innovants dans le domaine de la mobilité connectée et du Tire Digital Twin, et organisée en mode start-up au sein d’un grand groupe industriel. - Une première expérience dans les domaines attractifs de l’intelligence artificielle et de la modélisation de systèmes physiques, qui permettront au candidat d’appliquer et développer un large spectre de compétences dans un domaine exigeant en termes de données et de qualités des résultats attendus

michelin-clermont-ferrand::R-2026038976.desc: Trainee - - - - - - - - - - - - Durée du stage : 5 à 6 mois Début : A partir de Janvier 2027. Localisation : Michelin Innovation Park - Cataroux, à Clermont-Ferrand - France Contexte : Durant les prochaines décennies, l’évolution des technologies informatiques et des télécommunications transformera la mobilité : véhicules semi-autonomes ou autonomes, mobilité connectée et usages prédictifs de maintenance deviennent des enjeux centraux. Dans ce cadre, la compréhension et le suivi de l’évolution des propriétés des pneumatiques tout au long de leur vie est un élément clé pour assurer sécurité, performance et planification d’opérations de maintenance. Ces propriétés ne sont pas directement mesurables en conditions d'usage : elles doivent être reconstruites à partir de capteurs embarqués, de mesures indirectes et de la connaissance des phénomènes physiques mis en jeu (dynamique du véhicule, contact pneu-sol, mécanique et thermique du pneumatique). Les approches fondées sur des modèles physiques ou semi-physiques, associées à des méthodes d'estimation (filtrage, observateurs, identification de paramètres) et de traitement du signal, constituent ainsi un domaine majeur de recherche et d'ingénierie. Les méthodes statistiques et d'apprentissage peuvent venir compléter ces approches, dans une logique de modèles hybrides, sans se substituer à la compréhension physique. Le concept de Tire Digital Twin (Jumeau Numérique du Pneu), en complément de la mobilité connectée, offre un cadre pertinent pour développer des capacités prédictives et des outils d'aide à la décision. Il repose sur la fusion de mesures temporelles et de modèles physiques en continu, afin de suivre l'évolution des propriétés du pneumatique au cours de sa vie. Mission : Le stage permettra au/à la stagiaire de travailler sur le développement et l'évaluation de méthodes d'estimation et de traitement du signal appliquées aux pneumatiques et à leur usage. L'objectif est d'améliorer la robustesse et la précision des estimations et des prédictions de l'état du pneumatique, en exploitant des phénomènes physiques et en s'appuyant sur des signaux issus de capteurs embarqués. Principales activités : · Modélisation physique et semi-physique du pneumatique et de son comportement · Estimation d'état et de paramètres (filtrage, observateurs, identification) · Traitement du signal (analyse temporelle et fréquentielle, filtrage, extraction de caractéristiques) · Analyse des incertitudes et augmentation de la robustesse des estimations et des prédictions · Approches d'hybridation entre modèles physiques et méthodes « data-driven » (apprentissage automatique en complément) · Prétraitement et validation de données expérimentales (capteurs, essais, données de roulage) · Visualisation et communication des résultats Le/la stagiaire pourra : réaliser une revue bibliographique sur les méthodes d'estimation et de traitement du signal pertinentes, concevoir et implémenter des prototypes d'estimateurs (ou de chaînes de

Vous êtes en charge de : Contribuer à des projets innovants orientés sur des procédés de recyclage chimique ou d’ élaboration de polymères décalés ou de matières biosourcées Travailler en collaboration étroite avec les équipes de recherche, les équipes opérationnelles des sites pilotes et de production, ainsi qu’avec des partenaires universitaires ou industriels Définir les technologies répondant aux critères de performances techniques et industrielles, et concevoir les procédés ad hoc en évaluant leurs performances environnementales, techniques et économiques Piloter les collaborations externes nécessaires à la mission Construire, mettre en œuvre et piloter les études permettant d’atteindre les propriétés visées Assurer la mise en visibilité et la capitalisation des nouveaux savoirs et savoir-faire acquis, ainsi que la propriété intellectuelle associée aux nouvelles technologies Communiquer les résultats aux partenaires internes (concepteurs produits, chimistes, analystes, industrialisateurs…) Contribuer au progrès de l’activité : veille technologique, évolution digitale du métier, accompagnement technique des concepteurs juniors De formation Bac+5 ou Bac+8 en génie chimique / génie de procédé, vous avez au minimum 5 ans d’expérience significative dans le domaine de la conception et du développement de procédés chimiques. mycronic-taby::913.title: Director, Sales Americas
mycronic-taby::913.desc: The Sales Director, Americas, is the driving force behind our commercial expansion across the region. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Global Sales, you will own the Americas commercial agenda—translating high-level division strategy into focused market priorities and disciplined execution including yet not limited to commercial agenda owner, driving sustainable growth in system sales and partnering with aftermarket to expand customer lifetime value. This career opportunity is accountable for sales leadership, order intake, revenue, market share and commercial profit contribution. The Sales Director, Americas, translates division strategy into focused market priorities and disciplined execution. In this critical leadership role, you won't just manage a sales pipeline; you will shape the future of our business.

mycronic-taby::917.title: Quality Engineer
mycronic-taby::917.desc: We are seeking a talented Quality Engineer to oversee our quality assurance and continuous improvement initiatives across product lifecycles, supplier networks, and internal manufacturing processes. In this hands-on, high-impact role, you will take full ownership of quality assurance across the entire product lifecycle-from raw material inspection and supplier quality management to in-line manufacturing and final customer delivery. Utilizing data-driven methodologies, root cause analysis, and statistical process control, support a proactive quality culture, lead non-conformance investigations, and drive continuous improvement projects that directly influence operational efficiency and product excellence.

mycronic-taby::918.title: Senior Sales Manager, East Asia
mycronic-taby::918.desc: Surfx Mycronic is expanding its presence in Asia and seeking an experienced Senior Sales Manager, East Asia to drive business development and manage strategic customer relationships across Taiwan, Korea, Japan, and Hong Kong. This region represents a critical market for advanced packaging and Hybrid Bonding technologies, with a strong presence of leading foundries, memory manufacturers, OSATs, and bonding equipment OEMs, making it a key contributor to Surfx Mycronic’s long-term growth strategy. The Senior Sales Manager, East Asia will lead regional commercial activities, overseeing the full sales cycle from prospecting and opportunity development through customer evaluations, trials, contract negotiations, and order closure. The role will also be responsible for developing and maintaining strategic relationships across key accounts, Tier I manufacturers, and channel partner-served accounts to drive sustainable regional growth.

mycronic-taby::920.title: Field Applications Engineer (Fluid Dispensing)
mycronic-taby::920.desc: The Field Applications Engineer, Fluid Dispensing serves as a key customer‑facing technical expert, supporting demonstrations, system buyoffs, process development, and troubleshooting. In this role, you will work closely with customers throughout the entire engagement cycle-providing pre‑sales technical support, leading machine demonstrations and buyoffs, and delivering post‑sales assistance that ensures successful system performance. In addition, you will play a critical role in diagnosing and resolving machine issues, offering higher‑level process guidance, and building strong relationships with customers by helping them achieve optimal results with our fluid dispensing technologies. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys hands‑on engineering, problem‑solving, and working directly with customers to deliver innovative, high‑quality solutions. This role is located in Milwaukee, WI.

mycronic-taby::921.title: Field Applications Engineer (Fluid Dispensing)
mycronic-taby::921.desc: The Field Applications Engineer, Fluid Dispensing serves as a key customer‑facing technical expert, supporting demonstrations, system buyoffs, process development, and troubleshooting. In this role, you will work closely with customers throughout the entire engagement cycle-providing pre‑sales technical support, leading machine demonstrations and buyoffs, and delivering post‑sales assistance that ensures successful system performance. In addition, you will play a critical role in diagnosing and resolving machine issues, offering higher‑level process guidance, and building strong relationships with customers by helping them achieve optimal results with our fluid dispensing technologies. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys hands‑on engineering, problem‑solving, and working directly with customers to deliver innovative, high‑quality solutions. This role is located in San Jose, CA.

mycronic-taby::923.title: Field Service Engineer, SMT
mycronic-taby::923.desc: The Field Service Engineer, SMT, is responsible for providing technical expertise to customers; including working with customers to install, maintain and repair purchased products or services. This role will interface directly with customers, sales staff and various levels of management to manage, install and/or resolve system software and hardware failures, product performance issues and user quality improvements. Travel is required to perform the activities of this role and is anticipated but not limited to 50-75%. This role is located in Chicago, IL, Milwaukee, WI, or Minneapolis, MN.

mycronic-taby::922.title: Field Service Engineer, SMT
mycronic-taby::922.desc: The Field Service Engineer, SMT, is responsible for providing technical expertise to customers; including working with customers to install, maintain and repair purchased products or services. This role will interface directly with customers, sales staff and various levels of management to manage, install and/or resolve system software and hardware failures, product performance issues and user quality improvements. Travel is required to perform the activities of this role and is anticipated but not limited to 50-75%. This role is located in Baltimore, MD or Pittsburgh, PA.

mycronic-taby::882.title: Software Product Developer
mycronic-taby::882.desc: Your primary focus will be software development in Java, where you will contribute to enhancing existing features, modernising systems, and addressing technical challenges within an advanced product environment.

mycronic-taby::909.title: Manufacturing Technician III
mycronic-taby::909.desc: The Manufacturing Technician III will operate production equipment and be responsible for manufacturing and assembly of products. In this role, the Manufacturing Technician III will be able to work with other technicians as well as mechanical, electrical, and software engineers on a variety of electro-mechanical, optical and robotic projects.

mycronic-taby::629.title: Fitter/Machinist
mycronic-taby::629.desc: The Fitter/Machinist plays a vital role in the assembly and machining of RoBAT Ltd. precision electrical test machines. This hands-on position requires a high level of craftsmanship, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality.

mycronic-taby::758.title: Human Resources and Admin Supervisor
mycronic-taby::758.desc: The Human Resources & Admin Supervisor oversees all Human Resources and administrative processes, ensuring effective management and compliance with company policies and legal requirements. This role upholds organizational integrity by implementing Human Resources procedures and supporting global Human Resources initiatives. This role manages equipment and facilities, reception, property safety and maintenance, cleaning, and directing calls. This role also oversees daily operations and ensures the implementation and follow-up of new administrative projects. Additionally, this role supports travel arrangements, including VISA, tickets, and accommodation, and performs other ad-hoc duties as required and assigned. Beyond core Human Resources and administrative responsibilities, the Human Resources & Admin Supervisor fosters a culture of continuous improvement by streamlining processes and enhancing operational efficiency.

mycronic-taby::781.title: Vice President, Strategy & Business Development
mycronic-taby::781.desc: The Global Technologies division focuses on acquiring, incubating, and scaling high-potential niche technologies. The division operates a portfolio of independent, fast-growing business lines, with the objective of building leading positions in selected high-growth segments of the electronics industry. We are seeking a Vice President, Strategy and Business Development to drive long-term value creation across the Global Technologies portfolio. The role will be responsible for identifying and prioritizing the most attractive growth opportunities, shaping winning strategies, and ensuring successful execution from early-stage concepts through scalable, profitable business. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, working closely with the executive management, and business line leaders. It requires strong analytical capabilities, commercial judgment, and the ability to translate strategic direction into business outcomes across multiple markets and technologies.

mycronic-taby::795.title: Systems Architect
mycronic-taby::795.desc: Do you enjoy solving complex technical challenges and shaping the architecture of advanced products? As Senior Systems Architect within our Jet Printing-team, you will play a key role in defining the technical direction of our world-leading Jet Printing platform. Our stencil-free jet printing technology enables highly precise deposition of solder paste for advanced electronics manufacturing, setting new standards for flexibility, precision and performance.

mycronic-taby::805.title: Mechanical Engineer
mycronic-taby::805.desc: We are looking for a Mechanical Engineer, to join Mycronic's Global Technologies division working within our Applied Plasma business line (Surfx Technologies). It is an exciting time to join our team!

mycronic-taby::848.title: Software Development, Product & Technology Lead (m/f/d)
mycronic-taby::848.desc: The Software Development, Product & Technology Lead (m/f/d) combines strategic product management with engineering leadership. This position bridges market requirements and execution by defining the software vision, directing product roadmaps, and providing hands-on functional and line management to the Software Development team. Functioning as the central link between technical delivery and business stakeholders, this role drives the full software lifecycle, from requirement gathering to cross-functional releases, ensuring user-centered, high-quality software solutions.

mycronic-taby::853.title: Senior Lithography and Process Development Engineer
mycronic-taby::853.desc: Join Mycronic's Pattern Generators Division as a Senior Lithography & Process Development Engineer and play a key role in developing lithography processes for advanced semiconductor and display manufacturing. As part of the Metrology and Process Control group (PMCD), you will be responsible for driving process excellence through advanced process control, technology development, and continuous improvement. You will ensure robust, capable, and stable lithography processes while contributing to the development of future manufacturing technologies.

mycronic-taby::856.title: Testutvecklare SW/FW för automation och embedded systems
mycronic-taby::856.desc: Till teamet Electronics Design & Architecture (EDA) söker vi en Testutvecklare SW/FW för automation och embedded systems som vill ta en nyckelroll i att förbättra, utveckla och ansvara för test/verifiering av elektronik FW/SW och som säkerställer hög leveranskvalitet från elektronik till PG-produkternas kundsystemreleaser.

mycronic-taby::868.title: Master’s Thesis: Mechanical Stability Assessment of  Transducers for Acousto-Optic Deflectors
mycronic-taby::868.desc: How do you predict whether a complex multilayer thin-film structure will remain mechanically stable before it is manufactured? In this thesis, you will develop analytical/numerical models to evaluate stress, deformation and fabrication risks in piezoelectric transducers used in Mycronic's world-leading mask writers. The project combines materials science, thin-film mechanics and computational modelling, with the opportunity to create a reusable design methodology for future transducer designs.

mycronic-taby::870.title: Experienced Project Manager
mycronic-taby::870.desc: Mycronic is recruiting experienced Project Managers for its Pattern Generator division. In this role, you will lead product development throughout the entire product life cycle in a global, high-tech environment. The position combines project leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and responsibility for deliveries, resources, and budgets. Mycronic is looking for individuals who can prioritize effectively in a fast-changing environment, build strong relationships across all levels of the organization, and collaborate successfully with diverse teams. The ideal candidate is comfortable making independent decisions, has a background in technology development, and positive to contribute in improving methods, processes, and tools.

mycronic-taby::883.title: Master’s Thesis: Transferring large substrates in display photomask manufacturing
mycronic-taby::883.desc: Two master’s thesis students will research and develop innovative loading solutions for heavy display photomasks at Mycronic in Täby. The thesis project combines engineering design, stakeholder analysis, and concept evaluation, starting Spring 2027.

mycronic-taby::889.title: Project Manager
mycronic-taby::889.desc: The Project Manager is an experienced and highly motivated professional responsible for leading complex, custom-engineered capital equipment projects from order acceptance through installation, commissioning, and final customer acceptance. This highly visible, customer-facing role oversees the full project lifecycle, ensuring successful execution while maintaining alignment between customer expectations and internal teams. Through strong leadership, proactive problem-solving, and effective cross-functional collaboration, the Project Manager drives projects forward, resolves challenges, and delivers solutions that meet customer requirements and support long-term business relationships.

mycronic-taby::890.title: Business Director Probe Business (m/w/d)
mycronic-taby::890.desc: Objective of this position is to … … ensure the strategic, technological and operational advancement of atg Mycronic´s global probe business.

mycronic-taby::891.title: Materials Controller I
mycronic-taby::891.desc: The Material Controller I supports a variety of functions within the Supply Chain, with primary focus on the inventory management needs of the company. Interacting with all levels of the organization, self-starters with high energy, attention to detail, proficiency in material control and warehousing, along with related systems transaction capabilities will excel in this role.

mycronic-taby::897.title: Senior Strategic Financial Analyst
mycronic-taby::897.desc: The Senior Strategic Finance Analyst serves as a key strategic finance partner supporting divisional leadership across business performance management, financial planning, strategic initiatives, and M&A activities. The role reports into the Head of Finance and M&A and is responsible for conducting independent financial and operational analyses, developing executive-level presentations, identifying business opportunities and risks, and delivering actionable insights that support decision-making and long-term value creation. While your core domain lies in driving business performance and strategic finance, you will also have the high-impact opportunity to take part in acquisition evaluations, corporate due diligence, and post-M&A tracking.

mycronic-taby::903.title: Senior Semiconductor Equipment Engineer (Mechanical)
mycronic-taby::903.desc: The Senior Semiconductor Equipment Engineer is responsible for the design, development, and continuous improvement of automated plasma equipment for the semiconductor industry. This role leads mechanical engineering activities from initial concept and system design through prototyping, testing, validation, and product launch, applying strong expertise in mechatronics to develop high-precision, reliable equipment. The engineer works closely with electrical, controls, software, and process engineering teams to integrate complex systems and ensure equipment meets performance, quality, and reliability requirements. In collaboration with sales, service, and management, this role also supports troubleshooting, addresses technical challenges, and identifies opportunities to enhance equipment functionality, manufacturability, and overall performance.

mycronic-taby::902.title: Manager, R&D Engineering
mycronic-taby::902.desc: The Manager, R&D Engineering will lead the development and continuous improvement of Surfx Mycronic’s plasma technology and automated equipment platforms, translating advanced concepts into reliable, manufacturable, and scalable products for semiconductor manufacturing. This hands-on leadership role will oversee the full product development lifecycle, from concept and design through prototyping, testing, validation, and production release. The Manager, R&D Engineering, will provide technical guidance, develop engineering talent, strengthen product development processes, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure products meet performance, quality, reliability, and customer requirements while supporting Surfx Mycronic’s continued growth and long-term business goals.

mycronic-taby::904.title: Applications Service Engineer (Field Based)
mycronic-taby::904.desc: The Applications Service Engineer (Field Based) provides remote and on-site technical support to customers throughout the United States, Canada, and Mexico. This role combines technical expertise, analytical problem-solving, and customer service to support equipment repairs, process challenges, installations, and equipment optimization. The Applications Service Engineer (Field Based) serves as a trusted technical resource for customers by diagnosing and troubleshooting equipment issues remotely, providing on-site support when needed, and assisting with equipment installations and related technical activities.

nearfield-instruments-rotterdam::2672578.title: (Senior) IT/OT System Engineer
nearfield-instruments-rotterdam::2672578.desc: NFI is looking for a hands-on Senior Systems Administrator & Infrastructure Engineer to support and improve the Operational Technology (OT) environment within our products. This role focuses exclusively on the product control environment and does not cover corporate IT or site infrastructure. The ideal candidate has broad experience across physical server hardware, Windows Server, Linux, virtualization, networking, and storage, and is comfortable building, maintaining, and troubleshooting systems from the hardware level upward. This includes working with RAID, LVM, ZFS, Windows storage management, and Hyper-V, as well as diagnosing and replacing server components such as RAM, SSDs/HDDs, and other field-replaceable hardware. You will help keep product systems stable, secure, and supportable throughout their lifecycle. The product control architecture includes Windows and Linux servers, virtual machines, data storage, control boxes, industrial switches, firewalls, sensors, and machine communication networks. These components run product software, connect subsystems, protect network boundaries, and store operational and diagnostic data. We are looking for someone who understands how these components work together and can troubleshoot issues across software, operating systems, networking, virtualization, storage and machine communication layers. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1920681 Careers at NIST ASSOCIATE POSITIONS PREP Research Associate - Durability Assessment of Polymeric Materials Used in Civil Infrastructure Applications This position is part of the National Institute of Standards (NIST) Professional Research Experience (PREP) program. NIST recognizes that its research staff may wish to collaborate with researchers at academic institutions on specific projects of mutual interest and thus requires that such institutions be the recipients of a PREP award. The PREP program requires staff from a wide range of backgrounds to work on scientific research in many areas. Employees in this position will perform technical work that underpins the scientific research of the collaboration. Research Title: Postdoctoral Researcher on Civil Infrastructure Polymer Durability The work will entail: The PREP Researcher will conduct laboratory accelerating weathering exposure experiments on various polymer systems used in infrastructure applications, which will include building envelope materials, protective coatings, crack repair materials, and fiber reinforced polymer composite (FRP) retrofits. The PREP Researcher will help to identify select polymeric infrastructure materials in widespread use based on current limitations of these materials, identified research gaps, and identified durability issues. Accelerated weathering experiments will primarily take place on the state-of-the-art NIST SPHERE (Simulated Photodegradation via High Energy Radiant Exposure) device which allows precise control of temperature and relative humidity while exposing samples to highly uniform ultraviolet (UV) exposure. Other weathering exposure experiments in humidity chambers, a freeze/thaw chamber, a corrosion chamber, commercial UV-weathering devices, or at two outdoor weathering fields may be conducted. The PREP researcher will collect material property change data resulting from degradation and develop test configurations and methods to measure performance changes of an infrastructure material with respect to its given application (e.g., increased water penetration of a building envelope material). Alongside structural engineers, weathering data criteria will be collaboratively incorporated into design equations and structural models. Duties The successful applicant will design and fabricate micro- and nano-electronics in the NIST Boulder Microfabrication Facility. Key goals are to realize more sensitive and larger format sensor and readout circuits as well as the realization of new forms of sensors. The successful applicant will also support testing or perform testing of sensors and readout circuitry at ambient and cryogenic temperatures. The work location for this position is at the NIST campus in Boulder, Colorado. The research associate will also be encouraged to travel to present results at scientific conferences, attend collaboration meetings, and to commission new fabrication equipment. U.S. Citizenship is preferred for this position and U.S. Legal Permanent Residence is a minimum requirement. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1920181 Careers at NIST ASSOCIATE POSITIONS Bioformulation Digital Twin Developer This position is part of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Professional Research Experience Program (PREP). Individuals appointed through PREP perform technical work supporting collaborative scientific research between NIST and participating academic institutions. U.S. Citizen Preferred The Work Will Entail The associate will develop digital-twin-guided autonomous experimentation methods for soft-material and bioformulation systems. Working with the NIST Autonomous Formulation Laboratory , the associate will combine physics-grounded modeling, generative machine learning, automated formulation preparation, and multimodal characterization to connect formulation conditions, material structure, and measured properties. The research will focus on computational representations of three-dimensional structure and mesostructure and on virtual instruments that predict experimental observables from those representations. These models will be integrated with automated workflows that select informative experiments, reconcile measurements from multiple techniques, quantify uncertainty, and update the material digital twin. Relevant measurements may include small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering, resonant soft X-ray scattering, cryogenic electron microscopy, light scattering, spectroscopy, rheology, and related methods. Duties Develop, train, and validate generative and physics-informed models for the structure and behavior of soft-material and bioformulation systems. Create digital representations that connect formulation composition and processing conditions to material structure and predicted measurement results. Develop virtual instruments and inverse-modeling workflows that reconcile multimodal experimental data. Integrate digital-twin models with automated formulation and characterization workflows to guide experiment selection and model refinement. Incorporate uncertainty quantification, calibration, and validation methods so that computational predictions can be compared rigorously with experimental measurements. Define benchmarks for physical plausibility, reproducibility, structural diversity, and agreement with measured data. Produce documented code, datasets, metadata, model documentation, protocols, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1919496 Careers at NIST ASSOCIATE POSITIONS Statistical Methodology for AI Survey Response Detection and Analysis This position is part of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Professional Research Experience Program (PREP). NIST recognizes that its research staff may want to collaborate with researchers at academic institutions on specific projects of mutual interest and, therefore, requires those institutions to be recipients of a PREP award. The PREP program involves staff from a wide range of backgrounds conducting scientific research across various fields. Individuals in this position will perform technical work supporting the collaboration's scientific research. This project involves collaborative research working closely with NIST statisticians and social scientists to advance statistical survey methodology to address challenges presented by the widespread use of generative AI. The research will focus on methods for the detection of AI responses in online surveys and the analysis of survey data when such responses are suspected. The primary goals will include conducting simulation studies to assess the impact of AI responses, developing a robust theoretical framework for incorporating detection uncertainties directly into data analysis, and developing comprehensive guidance on best practices for survey practitioners at NIST. Duties Work with scientific collaborators to help define and clarify project goals and timelines. Conduct a systematic literature review of the state of the art in AI survey response detection. Use statistical modelling and simulation studies to quantify the impact of AI responses on survey findings. Implement statistical methods via a high-level programming language such as R or Python. Present and communicate of results and statistical analysis to non-statisticians. Required Skills, Expertise, and Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in statistics or a related quantitative field. Experience with data analysis and statistical simulation. Proficiency in at least one of R or Python. Strong oral and written communication skills. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1919506 Careers at NIST ASSOCIATE POSITIONS Transparent Performance Characterization of Measurement Systems in Forensics and Biology Developing and applying statistical methods to characterize the performance of forensic comparison methods in ways that are transparent and usable by non-statisticians. A central motivation is supporting the responsible adoption of algorithmic methods for comparing forensic evidence, such as cartridge case comparison. The goal is to provide information to help recipients assess what weight to give a particular comparison result, such as how method performance depending on conditions. Because forensic results ultimately inform the decisions of examiners, attorneys, judges, and jurors, the work emphasizes making the data and reasoning behind a performance claim visible and manipulable, so that recipients can form their own judgments rather than rely on an opaque summary or someone else’s sentiment. Across these projects you will quantify uncertainty in measures of discrimination and strength of evidence, design studies to assess potential sources of performance variability, evaluate metrics intended to capture evidence quality, and develop analyses, visualizations, and software tools that let non-specialists interrogate what drives method performance. A secondary thrust applies related ideas to measurement quality in other domains, such as the statistical analysis of live-cell monitoring data and creating analyses and tools supporting standards development for assessing the quality of cell-viability measurement systems. The balance between thrusts will depend on project needs and the candidate's strengths. Duties Developing statistical methods for quantifying uncertainty in the performance of measurement and comparison methods, accounting for potentially correlated data. Developing exploratory analyses, visualizations, and software tools that enable nonstatisticians to interrogate the factors that drive method and measurement-system performance. Designing studies and conducting analyses that characterize and apportion sources of variability in measured or reported performance Developing and evaluating metrics and standards for assessing quality, such as the quality of forensic comparisons or of cell-viability measurement systems Presenting results at internal meetings, and occasional meetings with external stakeholders. The primary project is a Testing and Evaluation (T&E) framework for generative AI watermarking, where the associate will lead the statistical analysis of evaluation results and develop the statistical engine behind NIST-CARAT (Calibrated Risk Assessment Tool for authentication technologies), an interactive tool enabling policymakers to explore the empirical performance consequences of compliance-threshold choices. The associate will actively participate in NIST measurement science and contribute to cutting-edge research and evaluation in generative AI. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/careers/associate-positions/1919516 Careers at NIST ASSOCIATE POSITIONS Uncertainty characterization of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning models Building a Python-based numerical sandbox that abstractly simulates a step-by-step sequential process representing modern manufacturing. The simulations will involve complex and irreversible systems, where early choices constrain later ones and outcomes are delayed. Distribution-free statistical theory and metrological discipline will be directly integrated into the evaluation of black-box deep learning architectures. The main goal is to design independent statistical oversight layers to monitor AI behavior and catch systemic errors under dataset shift. Specifically, the research will target two major AI failure modes: 1) Silent Overconfidence : This occurs when an AI operates on shifted out-of-distribution data but continues to output incorrect predictions with high mathematical certainty. You will develop independent tracking layers using advanced time series and multivariate monitoring methods to isolate small, sustained process drifts before they hit catastrophic boundaries.
