nvidia-alchemi-us::JR2029239.desc: NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing — with the GPU acting as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. Today, we are increasingly known as "the AI computing company". NVIDIA is hiring world class Software Engineers with AI Compiler and distributed systems experience for its Deep Learning Compiler Technology team. The team builds JaxPP, NVIDIA's open-source library for pipeline parallelism in JAX. JaxPP turns a JAX training program into per-stage tasks and runs them across many GPUs. With it, very large models can be trained on NVIDIA GPU clusters using unmodified JAX and XLA. Join the team that is developing advanced compiler and runtime technology for the entire deep learning community. What you'll be doing: Design and implement program transformations on JAX programs (jaxpr) for large-scale training, on top of unmodified JAX and XLA: pipeline schedules, placement of tasks across stages, sharding (including JAX explicit sharding), and overlap of communication with computation. Develop technologies and products involving optimizing compilers and runtime execution frameworks for accelerating deep learning training on large scale distributed systems. Work on compiling a graph intermediate representation (IR) to target specific code, and build the distributed runtime that dispatches per-stage programs to many GPUs and moves data between stages through communication libraries such as NCCL. Contribute to advancing the state of the art in compiler technology for delivering high performance on large-scale training workloads, including mixture-of-experts models. Collaborate with members of the software framework teams (for example JAX and XLA) and the hardware architecture teams to accelerate the next generation of deep learning software, and work on integrating JaxPP into JAX training frameworks, including MaxText. Be a core contributor to the open-source JaxPP project: keeping it working with new JAX releases, testing, performance tracking, and working with teams who adopt it for their training runs. Design and deploy AI-enabled debug and validation workflows used by the team — with explicit guardrails (evals, regression validation, false-positive handling) and measurable impact on cycle time, debug velocity, or escape rate. Translate complex silicon and system risk into decision-ready options for technical and executive audiences — without padding or hand-waving. nvidia-alchemi-us::JR2027731.desc: We are seeking a Mixed-Signal Engineer to work on analog–digital co-simulation and digital RTL design for a power controller. The digital RTL implements the full control loop, including protections, fault handling, and calibration. This is a unique role with complete system-level exposure and the opportunity to influence both analog and digital design. The engineer should be flexible as priorities shift between co-simulation, RTL development, and debugging. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can address, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work , to amplify human creativity and intelligence. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join our diverse team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world! What you'll be doing: Build and run co-simulations that connect digital RTL with analog circuits or SPICE and Verilog-A models. Enhance and maintain the RTL for the power controller’s full digital control loop. Verify startup, steady-state, transient, calibration, and fault behavior at the system level in either a purely digital or a co-simulation environment. Debug issues across the analog–digital boundary with analog and digital designers. Develop RTL behavioral models for mixed-signal blocks. Design and implement control, protection, fault-handling, and calibration features. What we need to see: B.S. or MS degree in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent experience) 1-3 years of work on analog–digital co-simulation and digital RTL design for a power controller. Experience designing and debugging synthesizable Verilog or SystemVerilog RTL. Flexibility to work across co-simulation and RTL design as project priorities change. A strong inclination to learn how the analog circuitry behaves. Analog expertise is not required; the team will provide support to help you ramp up. Strong teamwork and outstanding interpersonal skills. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience with digital control logic in power management or a related system. Strong knowledge of, or experience working with, mixed-signal and custom-designed IP solutions. Understanding of firmware and embedded controllers. Prior exposure to analog design and mixed-signal simulation. Together, let’s push the boundaries of innovation and make a lasting impact on the world. Make the choice, join our diverse team today! #LI-Hybrid

Take important part in definition of requirements for post-SI validation, as well as IC power and performance characterization. We offer an exciting work environment, with many new learning experiences and interactions with people from different aspects of the company. Our company employs some of the best engineers in the communication field from all across the world, working on innovative technology and developing new and daring projects. What we need to see: B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering/ Materials Engineering/Physics (or equivalent experience) with 5+ years of experience. Hands-on experience in analog and mixed-signal circuit characterization (e.g., PLLs, SerDes, ADCs/DACs, bandgap/reference circuits), including bench measurements and silicon debug. Strong problem-solving abilities and out of the box thinking. Work in a fast-paced, multifaceted work environment with a focus on technical excellence, innovative thinking and strong analytical skills are required. Ability to self-manage, show leadership, and have good social skills. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Prior Semiconductor Test engineering/VLSI validation experience. Hand on experience with scopes and lab equipment. Programming & Data analysis experience. Understanding of BE procedures and knowledge of power terminology and measurement methods. Power management characterization and reliability & validation engineering experience.

Drive architectural innovation by applying deep workload analysis to production machine learning frameworks. Track record of translating research findings and workload analysis into concrete software and hardware specifications that engineering teams acted on. Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++, applied to performance modeling, data analysis, and prototyping. nvidia-alchemi-us::JR2019758.desc: At NVIDIA, we are seeking exceptional engineers to join our autonomous driving team to design, implement, and deploy cutting-edge end-to-end autonomous driving systems, running on NVIDIA chips in mass-production vehicles. Our strategy has evolved from AI 1.0 — building a driver from scratch — to AI 2.0 — teaching an intelligent agent to drive. This next phase leverages LLMs, VLMs, and VLAs to bring unprecedented reasoning, planning capabilities, and interactivity with the driving system to autonomous vehicles and general robotics. Let’s build the future of autonomy—together! What You’ll Be Doing: Design and train innovative large-scale models—including generative, imitation, and reinforcement learning—to improve the planning and reasoning capabilities of our driving systems. Build, pre-train, and fine-tune LLM/VLM/VLA systems for deployment in real-world autonomous driving and robotics applications. Explore novel data generation and collection strategies to improve diversity and quality of training datasets. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deploy AI models in production environments, ensuring performance, safety, and reliability standards are met. Integrate machine learning models directly with vehicle firmware to deliver production-quality, safety-critical software. What We Need to See: Hands-on experience building LLMs, VLMs, or VLAs from scratch or a proven track record as a top-tier coder passionate about autonomous systems. Deep understanding of modern deep learning architectures and optimization techniques. Proven record of deploying production-grade ML models for self-driving, robotics, or related fields at scale. Strong programming skills in Python and proficiency with major deep learning frameworks. Familiarity with C++ for model deployment and integration in safety-critical systems. PhD with 2+ years, MS (or equivalent experience) with 4+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd: Experience with LLM/VLM/VLA systems deployable to autonomous vehicles or general robotics. Publications, open-source contributions, or competition wins related to LLM/VLM/VLA systems. Deep understanding of behavior and motion planning in real-world AV applications. Experience building and training large-scale datasets and models. Proven ability to optimize algorithms for real-time performance in resource-constrained environments and strong track record of taking projects from concept to production deployment. #AutonomousVehicles #deeplearning

THE ROLE

Physical engineering is one of the hardest domains for AI. Designs have to meet standards, calculations must be deterministic and checkable, and a wrong number can end up in a power system or a data centre. CurieOS is built to let agents do real engineering work and to show exactly how every output was produced.

The platform team builds the foundation that every workflow, agent and product on CurieOS depends on, and runs it in production for people who need to trust it. Your work sets the floor for how reliable our AI is, and the ceiling for what it can do.

This is a small team, and you'll shape what we build as well as how. You'll see the results of those decisions in production within days. If you want a narrow, well-defined slice of a large system, this isn't the role. If you want to own a platform while it scales, it is.




HOW WE WORK

We build with agents, not just for them. Everyone on the team works with the latest frontier models and coding agents every day, and token budgets won't hold you back. Part of what we build is CurieOS's ability to work on itself: triaging defects, proposing fixes and opening pull requests for engineers to review. So engineers here spend more of their time on design, review and judgement, and less on typing. If you already work this way, you'll feel at home. If you want to see how far it can go, this is the place to find out.

You'll also work alongside our AI researchers, turning cutting-edge research and evals into things that run in the platform and in production.

periodic-labs-us::0335ea7e-436c-4e50-a76.desc:
ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

We’re an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and an insatiable drive to push the boundaries of what’s scientifically possible.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Periodic Labs is building an AI that can simulate science and verify its own predictions — training on the full scientific method. Central to that mission is a high-throughput experimental materials science lab that handles hazardous chemistries, high-pressure and high-temperature processes, air-sensitive synthesis, toxic gas exposure risks, and an expanding suite of thin-film deposition tools including PVD, PLD and the complexity of what we run overnight and autonomously is increasing every month.

We believe EHS is integral to this ambition, not a compliance function bolted on after the fact, but a core design discipline that makes autonomous science possible. This EHS leadership role will build our safety architecture, defining permitting strategy, designing life safety systems, conducting process hazard analyses, and ultimately training our AI to reason about risk during experimental planning and execution.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead the site EH&S team through a hands-on approach to problem solving and operational support while promoting a strong safety and environmental culture. Ensure compliance with applicable EH&S regulations and standards, develop and improve programs aligned with company goals, and actively partner with lab and operations teams on day-to-day safety challenges. Own the digital EHS infrastructure, integrating inspections, training records, incident reporting, compliance tracking, KPI dashboards, action-item tracking, and audit workflows into a unified operational safety platform.

 - Own and manage all permitting processes with local, state, and federal agencies: Fire Department/CUPA via Accela, CERS submissions for hazardous materials, AQMD/BAAQMD air permits, and TSDF coordination for hazardous waste.

 - Maintain and update chemical inventory systems, SDS library, and hazard labeling in compliance with OSHA, CalEPA, and permitted MAQ thresholds including managing the expansion of our chemical inventory as new thin-film processes introduce HF-based wet chemistry, fluoride compounds, and specialty gases.

 - Lead Hazard Communication (HazCom) and SDS training programs for lab staff, including night shift and autonomous overnight operation protocols.

 - Coordinate EHS inspections and maintain required documentation and postings across both the existing powder lab and thin-film facility.

 - Design and review life safety systems, including fire suppression, e-stop networks, gas detection (including toxic gas alarms for HF, H2Se, and other process chemistries), interlocks, alarm interfaces, and emissions/waste abate

ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

Periodic Labs is an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, semiconductors, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and an insatiable drive to push the boundaries of what’s scientifically possible.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Periodic Labs is building AI systems that can simulate physical science, verify predictions, and train on the full scientific method. We are looking for a Computational Scientist to develop structural, thermal, and coupled thermo-mechanical simulation capabilities for semiconductor systems and advanced materials.

This role is for someone who thinks of themselves as both a scientist and a software engineer. You understand solid mechanics and heat transfer at a level that goes beyond configuring a commercial FEA package, and you are comfortable building, extending, or automating solvers when the physics or scale of the problem requires it.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Develop agent-based structural and thermal simulation capabilities for semiconductor systems, including wafer stress and warpage, thin-film residual stress, thermo-mechanical reliability, thermal budget modeling, process-induced deformation, fracture and delamination, and coupled heat-stress problems.

 - Build or extend custom solvers where commercial FEA tools are too slow, too opaque, or insufficiently flexible. This may include custom FEM implementations, phase-field fracture models, crystal plasticity codes, thin-film mechanics frameworks, or reduced-order mechanical models, written in Python, C++, or Julia.

 - Model materials behavior at the level the physics requires: elasticity, plasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, fracture, diffusion-induced stress, thermal expansion mismatch, interfacial mechanics, and materials evolution under process conditions.

 - Validate models against experimental measurements including wafer metrology, curvature and bow measurements, DIC, profilometry, nanoindentation, or failure analysis data.

 - Design and curate evaluation datasets in collaboration with RL researchers to train LLMs capable of directing complex simulation pipelines.

 - Generate simulated datasets for ML training in regimes where experimental coverage is expensive or difficult to achieve.

 - Build and automate simulation pipelines at scale, architecting workflows that connect simulation outputs to data infrastructure, ML systems, and autonomous experimentation loops.

Periodic Labs is building an autonomous laboratory for high-throughput materials discovery. Our work combines advanced chemistry, robotics, automation, AI, and materials science to accelerate scientific discovery while maintaining high standards of environmental, health, and process safety.

We are seeking a hands-on, highly organized EHS Technician to support day-to-day laboratory safety operations, hazardous waste management, chemical inventory, compliance activities, and laboratory readiness.

Working closely with the EHS Engineer, Facilities team, scientists, and technicians, you will help execute the laboratory’s EHS programs and keep the facility safe, compliant, organized, and inspection-ready.

About Periodic Labs

We’re an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and an insatiable drive to push the boundaries of what’s scientifically possible.

As a Research Engineer, Semiconductor, you’ll own device-level validation of our materials work, taking novel thin-film stacks from deposition through patterned test vehicles to measure electrical performance. You’ll design and run short-loop experiments that demonstrate how materials and interfaces translate into device behavior, leveraging both internal and external lab resources. You’ll also contribute technical expertise to customer-facing engagements, and this role blends deep hands-on capability with the flexibility to work across teams and partners to solve hard materials problems.

 - Connect materials and interface properties to device outcomes, feeding insights back into film-stack and process development.

 - Document experimental methodology, results, and learnings to feed both internal knowledge and AI training infrastructure.

 - Strong command of device physics and integration flows, with a track record of demonstrating device performance in short-loop test vehicles.

 - Hands-on fabrication experience spanning lithography (photo, laser direct-write, or e-beam), thin-film deposition, etch, and metrology.

 - A deep understanding of how materials selection and interface quality drive device performance.

 - Proficiency in probe-station device measurement, plus the ability to architect and assemble custom electrical test setups.

periodic-labs-us::19e2cc72-0f04-44b3-a9c.title: Process Technician, Thin Films
periodic-labs-us::19e2cc72-0f04-44b3-a9c.desc:
ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

Periodic Labs is building an autonomous laboratory for high-throughput materials discovery. Our work combines advanced chemistry, robotics, automation, AI, and materials science to accelerate scientific discovery while maintaining high standards of environmental, health, and process safety.


About the Role
Periodic Labs is building AI that can both simulate science and verify its own predictions. Verifying those predictions experimentally requires a lab that runs reliably - qualified tools, samples prepared to spec, and data logged the same way every time.

We are standing up a dedicated thin-film lab in Menlo Park with a suite of deposition and characterization tools, and are hiring a Process Technician to own day-to-day tool operation, sample preparation, and first-line maintenance. This is the role that keeps throughput high and variance low: you run the SOPs, you cut and prep the coupons, you keep the tools in spec, and you partner with process engineers when an experiment calls for something outside the standard flow.

This is a contract position, on-site, with the possibility of extension or conversion as the lab scales.


What You'll Do

 - Run deposition tools to SOP. Execute recipes on vacuum-based thin-film deposition systems. Load and unload, verify chamber state and process conditions, confirm the run matched setpoints, and log the result.

 - Prepare samples. Dice and cleave coupons from full wafers; handle mounting and cross-section prep for imaging. Clean and prep substrates per workflow-specific recipes — wet cleans, oxide strip, dehydration bake, substrate and source conditioning.

 - Operate characterization tools. Collect and log structural, optical, and electrical film data. Recognize when a scan, fit, or image indicates a tool problem rather than a material result, and escalate rather than re-run blind.

 - Perform first-line and preventive maintenance. Chamber opens and cleans, source and consumable changes, shield and liner swaps, pump-down and leak checks, calibration checks, and PM scheduling. Work with vendors and facilities on service visits and keep maintenance history complete.

 - Keep the tools qualified. Run qual and monitor samples on a set cadence, track thickness, uniformity, and rate against baseline, and flag drift early. Maintain SPC-style charts where they exist and help build them where they don't.

 - Support non-standard work. When engineers need a one-off — an unusual stack, an off-recipe parameter sweep, a new substrate geometry, an unproven prep sequence — you help scope what the tool can safely do, run it, and document what actually happened.

 - Document everything. Every run is a potential data point for our models. Record what you did rather than what the recipe said, capture failures and fixes alongside successes, and meet the metadata standards our data pipeline depends on.

periodic-labs-us::e82a30cb-ad71-402f-b1c.desc:
ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

Periodic Labs is an AI and physical sciences company in Menlo Park, CA. We run an in-house materials synthesis and characterization lab alongside our research teams.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced diffraction specialist to manage our X-ray diffraction facility, which includes multiple laboratory diffractometers used for powder, thin-film, and capillary measurements. You will be responsible for instrument alignment and calibration, preventive maintenance and repair, user training, measurement standards, radiation safety, and overall attention to the performance of the X-ray equipment.

You will also help specify and commission new instruments, write the SOPs and qualification protocols the group works from, and work with our software team so that instrument data and metadata are recorded consistently. You will work daily with scientists, technicians, and engineers across synthesis, software, and research.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Instrument alignment, calibration, configuration control, and uptime across the facility, including the criteria used to decide whether an instrument is ready for use.

 - Reference standards and quality control: maintain house standards and a regular QC schedule so that the same standard gives consistent results across instruments

 - Difficult measurements: non-routine geometries, weakly scattering or air-sensitive samples, thin films, and non-ambient stages, with attention to distinguishing instrument artifacts from real effects.

 - Maintenance and repair: troubleshooting and preventive maintenance; coordination of service contracts and vendor visits when needed.

 - Commissioning new instruments: site preparation, acceptance testing, and comparison against existing instruments.

 - User training: train and certify scientists and technicians, review early runs, and provide support.

 - Documentation and data: maintain SOPs, measurement recipes, and data-reduction conventions; ensure raw data, instrument state, calibration status, and sample metadata are recorded consistently and in a structured format.

 - Radiation safety: X-ray equipment registration and compliance, interlock testing, surveys, along with compressed gas and cryogen handling for non-ambient stages.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience operating and maintaining X-ray diffractometers in a university shared facility, national lab, analytical services lab, industrial R&D lab, or at an instrument vendor.

 - Strong XRD background across powder, thin-film, and capillary/transmission work. Proficient in phase identification, Rietveld refinement, and quantitative analysis.

 - Experience maintaining several instruments, ideally from more than one vendor. Comfortable troubleshooting hardware and judging when to repair versus call for service.

 - Careful documentation habits; treats metadata as part of the measurement.

 - Able to support many users in a busy lab while maintaining good practice.

We are building a dedicated thin-film lab while generating early data at partner facilities.

We're looking for a hands-on Postdoctoral Associate in Thin Films to run advanced deposition and nanofabrication processes, generate high-quality experimental data, and collaborate closely with our AI and materials teams. periodic-labs-us::20b122c9-b8ec-4fb0-aaf.desc:
ABOUT PERIODIC LABS

We're an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and a drive to push the boundaries of what's scientifically possible.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're training frontier models to develop deep scientific knowledge and reasoning for scientific tasks. You’ll study how RL scales with training compute, develop better algorithms, and take ideas from controlled experiments to our largest runs like Periodic Neon https://periodic.com/news/nature-is-our-learning-environment.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design experiments to understand how RL performance scales with compute, model size, data, and reward quality, building on work such as ScaleRL https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13786

 - Develop better RL algorithms, spanning policy optimization, advantage estimation, exploration, and credit assignment for long-horizon RL tasks

 - Build adaptive sampling and curriculum methods that adjust task difficulty, problem selection, and the number of rollouts as models improve

 - Study bias and stability during RL training, including importance-sampling corrections  and methods to tackle policy staleness and training–inference mismatch, as discussed here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GH4JCdAAUYg.

 - Improve compute efficiency across training and inference through experiments with hyperparameters, such as length penalties, rollout counts, batch sizes, and update schedules.




YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Hands-on experience training LLMs with reinforcement learning

 - Strong attention to detail and rigorous approach to answer questions scientifically.

 - Coming up with small-scale RL setups that transfers to large-scale training runs.

 - Comfort working across a complex training stack to implement, debug, and test new research ideas.

 - We are open to offering a 1 year post-doc for this profile. Early career (final year PhD students) are encouraged to apply.

We’re an AI and physical sciences company building state-of-the-art models to accelerate breakthroughs across materials, energy, and beyond. Backed by world-class investors and growing rapidly, we operate at the pace the frontier requires. Our team brings deep expertise, genuine ownership, and an insatiable drive to push the boundaries of what’s scientifically possible.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Periodic Labs is building an AI that can simulate science and verify its own predictions — training on the full scientific method. Central to that mission is a high-throughput experimental materials science lab that handles hazardous chemistries, high-pressure and high-temperature processes, air-sensitive synthesis, toxic gas exposure risks, and an expanding suite of thin-film deposition tools including PVD and PLD. The complexity of what we run overnight and autonomously increases every month.

We believe EHS is integral to this ambition, not a compliance function bolted on after the fact, but a core design discipline that makes autonomous science possible. This role focuses on operational safety: making sure every new process, tool, and autonomous workflow is hazard-reviewed, safe to start up, and safe to run around the clock. You will also help train our AI to reason about risk during experimental planning and execution.





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Partner with automation and controls teams to implement machine safeguarding, fail-safes, interlocks, robotics safety controls, functional safety validation, safety PLC reviews, and automated motion hazard assessments for autonomous experimental systems.

 - Develop and maintain EHS standards, specifications, procedures, and governance systems that can scale across multiple facilities.

 - Collaborate with ML/AI engineers on training an LLM to reason through process hazards, risk assessments, and safety constraints during experimental planning and autonomous execution — making EHS a first-class input to our AI’s decision-making.

 - Provide technical expertise in high-throughput R&D with a strong focus on chemical safety, including the thin-film lab's specialty gas delivery, vacuum, and RF/high-voltage systems. .

 - Lead incident investigations and root cause analyses, own injury reporting and recordkeeping (Cal/OSHA 300 log, serious-injury reporting), and drive corrective actions to closure.

Join our PIC Design & Development team and help shape the next generation of photonic computing. Your role As Senior Photonic Engineer for Modulator Design, you own the design of TFLN electro-optic modulators. These are the core building blocks of our PICs, and their performance directly sets the speed and energy efficiency of our products. You are the technical anchor for all modulator design decisions within the PIC team. q-ant-stuttgart::2635736.title: Senior RF / Analog Design Engineer (m/f/d)
q-ant-stuttgart::2635736.desc: The future of AI computing is light, not electrons. Q.ANT is building photonic processing systems that compute with light – delivering a scalable, energy-efficient alternative to transistor-based architectures for next-generation AI and HPC applications. As Senior GHz Analog & Mixed-Signal Engineer (m/f/d) , you are the architect of the high-speed electronic signal paths in the GHz-range that make photonic computing real. You will design, simulate, and validate circuits that interface directly with cutting-edge silicon photonic devices, custom ASICs, and advanced 2.5D/3D interposer platforms. Working at the intersection of RF electronics, electro-optics, and semiconductor heterogeneous integration , you will turn individual high-performance components into unified, scalable subsystems. Your Responsibilities High-Speed Analog & Mixed-Signal Design: Specify, design, and simulate GHz-band circuits including TIAs, ADC/DAC front-ends, amplifiers, and PLLs – optimizing for noise, linearity, jitter, bandwidth, and power efficiency using tools such as SPICE, SpectreRF, and ADS. Electronic-Photonic Co-Design: Define and optimize electrical-optical impedance matching, biasing, and signal conditioning for silicon photonic components including modulators, photodetectors, and waveguide interfaces. Interposer & Advanced Packaging Integration: Develop and validate 2.5D/3D integration architectures using interposers and chiplets; co-simulate RF parasitics, TSV routing, and thermal behavior to ensure signal integrity across heterogeneous boundaries. ASIC Collaboration: Partner with ASIC designers to define high-speed interface requirements and support SerDes, CDR, and mixed-signal block integration. Lab Bring-Up & Validation: Lead hands-on characterization of electro-optic bandwidth, eye diagrams, jitter, noise spectra, and system-level behavior using oscilloscopes, VNAs, BERTs, and spectrum analyzers. Innovation & IP Contribution: Propose novel analog architectures and co-integration strategies that push beyond conventional design limits, contributing to Q.ANT's IP portfolio and next-generation photonic processor roadmap. Educational Foundation: M.S. or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Microsystems Engineering, or a related technical field. Industry Expertise: 5+ years designing analog/mixed-signal circuits in the 1–20 GHz range, with strong command of SPICE/Spectre, ADS, HFSS, and S-parameter/EM co-simulation. Electro-Optic Experience: Hands-on background integrating electronics with silicon photonic or optoelectronic components – modulators, photodiodes, optical packaging – is a strong advantage. Packaging & SI/PI Know-How: Demonstrated experience with high-speed PCB design, signal and power integrity analysis, and advanced packaging concepts (CoWoS, EMIB, or similar). Analytical Toolset: Familiarity with Python or MATLAB for measurement automation and data analysis; experience defining test SOPs for reproducibility. Language: Fluent English required;

radical-ai-us::caaac405-c8a5-4daa-ae6d-0.title: Director of Software Engineering
radical-ai-us::caaac405-c8a5-4daa-ae6d-0.desc:
Radical AI is replacing an R&D process that currently takes 10+ years and $100 million to produce a single discovery. Our self-driving lab platform combines AI with autonomous robotics to run experiments, analyze results, and iterate—continuously, without human bottlenecks. For industries like aerospace, automotive, defense, energy, manufacturing, semiconductors, and space, that means breakthroughs in weeks instead of years.

We're a small, senior team, growing fast. This is a foundational hire.




The Role
We're looking for a Director of Software Engineering to build and lead the software engineering team as we scale. This is a player-coach role in the truest sense: you'll ship code every week while also owning the team's growth, culture, processes, and long-term technical direction.
You'll report to our President and Co-Founder, and work closely with cross-functional stakeholders across science, hardware, and product. The immediate mandate is to stabilize and grow a talented but lean team during a period of rapid hiring and technical expansion — including near-term customer deployments that involve significant architectural challenges.
This is not a role for someone who wants to delegate the hard technical problems. It's for someone who wants to be in the middle of them.

The Role
This is a generalist software engineering role on the team building the core platform that powers our autonomous lab. Depending on where you plug in, you might own backend services, agent tooling, data and orchestration pipelines, internal platforms, or the infrastructure that keeps our systems observable and reliable in production.
 
What's non-negotiable: strong systems thinking, production instincts, and the ability to contribute across the stack. We're building software that controls and monitors physical systems in the real world — the bar for correctness and reliability is high.
 
We work across a deeply cross-disciplinary domain (robotics, ML, experimental automation), and one near-term priority involves hybrid cloud/on-prem deployments in customer environments. Engineers who've navigated those constraints will hit the ground running.

At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary A CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) Process Engineer is responsible for the critical semiconductor manufacturing step of planarizing the wafer surface. This is achieved through a synergistic combination of chemical reactions and mechanical force, ensuring that subsequent layers of the chip can be built with high precision. The primary goal of a CMP engineer is to achieve a flat wafer surface by controlling the chemical reaction and mechanical force. Role and Responsibilities Here's What You'll Be Responsible For: Removal Rate (RR) Control: Conducting performance evaluations of various influence factors to ensure the thickness skew before and after CMP is consistent across the entire wafer. Condition Optimization: Determining the optimal process conditions to improve uniformity and resolve chronic issues, such as "center low RR profiles. Recipe Management: Developing and optimizing Recipe (RCP) parameters and improve flatness. Defect & uniformity Management: Managing and improving wafer uniformity and resolving defects such as scratches and particles. Consumable Life Cycle Management: Monitoring the usage cycles of consumables (pads, slurry) to ensure they do not exceed specifications, which could impact quality. Material Evaluation: Evaluating the performance of different slurries and polishing pads to optimize the CMP process. Skills and Qualifications Here's What You'll Need: Basic requirement BS or MS in Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Material Science, or Computer Science. A minimum 5 years of related experience; Semiconductor Process Flows. Previous experience in a high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environment desired. Applicable manufacturing experience in other industries can be considered. Basic CMP Knowledge: Understanding of dielectric and metal CMP fundamentals, including slurry-pad-conditioning interactions and post-clean steps. Prefer to have some level of Equipment Familiarities: Hands-on experience with major industry CMP tools: AMAT/EBara and their end point systems Data & Statistics: Proficiency in Statistical Process Control (SPC), Fault Detection and Classification (FDC), and analysis software like JMP or Spotfire. Problem Solving: Ability to drive root-cause analysis using methodologies like FMEA, 8D, and first-principles physics approaches. Flexibility: As per business needs, sometimes it is required to work during off-hour times and/or with CWW shift schedule. Preferred Qualifications Familiar with Metrology Tools: Experience with Ellipsometry, SEM, and AFM for thickness and roughness check. samsung-austin-semiconductor-usa::R12164.desc: About Samsung Austin Semiconductor Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary As an Etch Engineer - Process Owner, see roles and responsibilities below. Role and Responsibilities Develop and optimize Front End of Line (FEOL) and Back End of Line (BEOL) plasma etch processes for emerging Gate-All-Around (GAA) architectures including 2 nm node and mature semiconductor technology nodes, including 14nm, 17nm, 28nm FinFET. Implement and sustain Advanced Process Control (APC) methodologies, including feed-forward (FF) process control strategies for trench etch and via-height optimization. Perform Statistical Process Control/Fault Detection and Classification (SPC/FDC) monitoring, statistical yield analysis, and root-cause investigations for plasma etch process excursions, interlocks, and Out-of-Control Action Plan (OCAP) events. Qualify and integrate heterogeneous etch tool platforms, including LAM Research FLEX/KIYO, and/or TEL, Applied Materials, Mattson, PSK and SEMES and cross-platform etch equipment for production deployment. Conduct process matching and technology transfer activities across global semiconductor manufacturing sites. Support factory ramp-up activities through tool qualification planning, capacity optimization, and throughput improvement initiatives. Develop monitoring plans for post-preventive maintenance (PM) defect detection and production wafer qualification. Collaborate with equipment engineering, process integration, metrology, and yield enhancement teams to improve process stability and manufacturing efficiency. Utilize DOE methodologies and statistical analytics platforms, including Spotfire, JMP, Minitab, and Python for process optimization and defect reduction initiatives. Perform failure analysis and material characterization using SEM, EDX, spectroscopy, and related semiconductor characterization techniques. Position Summary The Yield Analysis & Improvement role is a critical technical leadership position focused on maximizing semiconductor manufacturing efficiency and product quality. The primary objective is to own end-to-end yield performance across wafer sort, parametric, and final testing. By leveraging advanced data mining, statistical analysis, and machine learning, the role identifies key yield limiters and develops automated analytics pipelines to correlate electrical failures with inline defect data, ensuring a seamless transition from technology launch to mass production ramp. Beyond data analysis, this role serves as a central hub for cross-functional collaboration. The engineer partners with Process Integration, Module, and Design teams to optimize process windows, reduce variability, and resolve layout-dependent issues. Utilizing structured problem-solving methodologies and partnering with Failure Analysis (FA) teams for physical and electrical correlation, the role drives the root cause investigation and corrective actions necessary to contain yield excursions and improve overall manufacturability. At the staff level, the role expands into strategic yield management and organizational leadership. This involves defining the long-term yield roadmap, establishing key performance indicators (KPIs), and leading high-priority task forces to resolve critical production risks. Furthermore, the position is responsible for mentoring junior engineers and interfacing with executive leadership to provide transparent insights into the health and risks of the fabrication process. Role and Responsibilities Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For: Yield Analysis & Improvement Own end-to-end yield performance across wafer sort, parametric test, and final test. Perform advanced data mining and statistical analysis to identify yield limiters and drive improvement actions. Generate yield detractors and correlate yield to electrical, inline, and defect data. Process & Technology Optimization Collaborate with process integration and module teams to reduce variability and improve process windows. Define and execute defect reduction strategies. Partner with Module and Process Integration engineers to solve complex critical defect issues. Support technology launch, ramp, and transfer across nodes and fab. Root Cause & Failure Analysis Lead root cause investigations using structured problem-solving methodologies. Partner with FA teams (EFA/PFA) to correlate physical defects with electrical signatures. Collaborate with Design and Product teams to ensure manufacturability and resolve layout-dependent yield issues before mass production ramp. Drive containment and corrective actions

We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. You Are You have spent years keeping the infrastructure running that everyone else depends on to do their jobs, and you know that when a license server goes down at 3 a.m. in Tokyo, someone's tapeout schedule just became your problem. You are the person who can look at a FlexNet debug log, spot the misconfigured options file or the firewall rule that is blocking port 27000, and have it fixed before the customer finishes explaining what went wrong. You do not just troubleshoot, you think in systems. You understand how a three-server redundant licensing setup should behave, why a migration from on-prem to cloud changes the MAC address binding, and what happens when someone upgrades RHEL without testing the environment variables first. You have been in enough customer environments to know that "it worked in dev" means nothing until it works in production. You are comfortable talking to a senior CAD engineer about daemon logs and then turning around to explain to a procurement lead why their license count does not match their headcount. You move fast, you document what you learn, and you do not wait for perfect information to start solving the problem. At Synopsys, you will work with global customers who depend on you to keep their design environments operational, and the problems you solve will directly enable the next generation of chips. Play Video Job Description Date posted 11/12/2026 Category Engineering Hire Type Employee Job ID 19425 Remote Eligible No Date Posted 11/12/2026 The Synopsys Digital IP R&D team is hiring experienced ASIC/IP Verification Engineers (2 to 5 years) to work on advanced connectivity protocols, including Ethernet / UFS / UniPro / USB / MPhy, across commercial, enterprise, and automotive applications. Job Role What You'll Be Doing: Be part of the Synopsys IP Verification R&D team at our Bangalore R&D Center, working closely with the RTL design team within a global team of expert Verification Engineers Contribute to end-to-end verification of subsystems with high-speed interconnect IPs, including one or more of controllers and Phy IP related to protocols such as Ethernet / UFS / UniPro / USB / MPhy, from test planning to coverage closure and sign-off Develop and use state-of-the-art verification environments for the Synopsys IP family of synthesizable cores, and perform verification tasks on these IP cores Understand compliance testing standards and build simulation-based compliance test suites Develop SystemVerilog/Verilog testbenches and test cases; run regressions, analyze coverage, and debug failures using methodologies such as UVM and formal verification Cover test planning, unit-level and system-level test environment coding, test case coding and debugging, Controller-PHY IP interoperability testing, and regression management Beyond traditional verification, you’ll have the opportunity to work with frontier AI models and build agentic workflows for verification, from automated testbench creation and test planning to coverage analysis and closure. Contribute to IP development used in high-performance computing, communications, servers, consumer devices, and automotive applications that power the technologies of tomorrow Collaborate across design, architecture, and validation teams and drive issues to resolution Requirements: What You'll Need: Engineering degree / Post graduation (B.Tech / M.Tech) with 2–5 years of verification experience Hands on experience with coding in Verilog, System Verilog and methodology such as UVM Controller–PHY integration / interoperability simulation experience is a strong plus Prior experience in usa

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

The Team 
The long-term vision of TRI’s Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery (AMDD) program is to accelerate the development of truly emissions-free mobility. Realizing this vision will require the discovery of new materials and devices for batteries, fuel cells, and more. Our aim at TRI is to merge sophisticated computational materials modeling, new experimental data, artificial intelligence, and automation to significantly accelerate materials research in this area. Our focus is on developing tools and capabilities to enable this acceleration. We collaborate closely with a dozen universities and national labs and our colleagues across global Toyota. AMDD seeks to develop and translate the newest technologies into practice, both within Toyota and the open research community, more broadly.
 
This Internship
We are looking for an intern researcher to contribute to the development of atomistic catalysis modeling that bridges the gap between current simulation (e.g. DFT) and in-situ catalysis experiments. We will develop reasoning models with embedded chemical and atomistic descriptors as well as experimental parameters and measurements. Your day-to-day may include: literature review of computational methods and model construction and validation. We welcome you to join a unique team of scientists and engineers where you will constantly learn new skills at the interface of materials science and thoughtful

The Team
 
The long-term vision of TRI’s Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery (AMDD) program is to accelerate the development of truly emissions-free mobility. Realizing this vision will require the discovery of new materials and devices for batteries, fuel cells, and more. Our aim at TRI is to merge cutting-edge computational materials modeling, experimental data, artificial intelligence, and automation to significantly accelerate materials research. Our focus is on developing tools and capabilities to enable this acceleration. We collaborate closely with a dozen universities and national labs and colleagues across global Toyota. AMDD seeks to develop and translate the newest technologies into practice, both within Toyota and the open research community more broadly.

The Internship
 
We are seeking a research intern to develop algorithms and computational systems for multi-agent learning and coordination. The central question is how agents with different data and capabilities can share information, build predictive models, and select computational tasks that improve their collective understanding of data. Potential approaches include distributed and federated learning, as well as information-theoretic methods for communication and task selection. The intern will implement and benchmark these methods, evaluating how coordination affects model accuracy, communication costs, and computational efficiency. Relevant interests include machine learning, multi-agent systems, distributed computing, and information theory.

We’re looking for a researcher/engineer interested in how machine learning models represent molecules and materials, and whether different models discover the same underlying physical structure. The Automated Driving Advanced Development division bridges TRI research and Toyota products. In partnership with Woven by Toyota, the team is researching and developing an end-to-end learned driving stack that maps sensor inputs directly to planned trajectories.
The Internship
We’re seeking a research intern to investigate how driving policies post-trained in fast, low-fidelity simulation can transfer to higher-fidelity simulation and real-world driving. This is an open research problem: differences in sensor inputs, vehicle dynamics, and other agents can limit transfer, and policies may learn simulator-specific behavior or forget previously learned skills.
You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. You’ll work with Toyota driving data, generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure, with the goal of producing work suitable for a conference or workshop submission.
The Opportunity
As a research intern on AD2, you will own a standalone research project in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, with the opportunity to:
Drive your own research: Shape the approach, run experiments, and analyze results, with the independence to set your own direction.
Publish your findings: The project is designed to produce results suitable for a conference or workshop publication.
Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles.
Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving.
Work at scale: Use the same large-scale Toyota driving data, base models, and simulation infrastructure the team uses every day.
You can learn more about our work on the Automated Driving Advanced Development team page.

The Opportunity
We are seeking a research intern to advance continual adaptation for robot policies. Our goal is to enable robots to improve from experience, personalize their behavior, preserve learned capabilities, and build on prior learning to acquire new behaviors more efficiently.
You will work closely with our robotics and machine learning researchers on a project shaped around your interests, expertise, and the team’s priorities. The work will combine algorithm development with experiments in simulation and on real robots, emphasizing reliable adaptation with limited robot experience and human effort.
The Research
We are interested in how robots can improve through ongoing experience while preserving and building on what they have learned. Your project could explore one of the following directions:
Continual learning: Preserve existing capabilities through successive adaptations and use prior experience to learn new behaviors more efficiently. Investigate how useful adaptations can be retained, combined, and reused, including settings where the original training data are unavailable.
Efficient learning and adaptation: Enable robots to improve with limited experience by identifying where adaptation is needed and making effective use of prior knowledge, new interactions, and guidance.
Personalization from human guidance: Use demonstrations, corrections, or preference feedback to change how a robot performs a task while maintaining task success. Investigate when guidance is sufficient and when further learning is needed.
Possible approaches include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, agentic tool use, modular policies, and distillation, depending on the research question.

We envision a future where robots assist with household chores and cooking, aid older individuals in maintaining their independence, and enable people to spend more time on the activities they enjoy most. Our mission is to answer the question “What will it take to create truly general-purpose robots that can accomplish a wide variety of tasks in settings like human homes with minimal human supervision?” We believe that the answer lies in using large-scale datasets of physical interaction from a variety of sources and building on the latest advances in machine learning to learn general-purpose robot behaviors from this data.
The Internship
We are seeking a research intern to join our Human Aware Interaction and Learning (HAIL) team. The research conducted on this internship aligns with our broader mission and will focus on one or more of the following areas at the intersection of robot learning and human-robot interaction (HRI):
Data-efficient and general algorithms for learning robust multimodal policies that can also reason over actions in the presence of a human. This research would examine what additional features should be modeled when humans are present in the scene, or in collaborative scenarios, including how roles are shared and reallocated between the human and the robot.
Developing hierarchical reasoning frameworks for learned robot policies that can reason over human and shared task states (intent, cues, roles) in order to enable fluent human-robot collaboration.
Robustifying data-driven robot policies to the presence of humans, particularly in the low-data regimes typical of HRI, including approaches for data aggregation and simulative approaches towards adaptation of vision-language-action (VLA)  models to human-human and/or human-robot interaction datasets.
Uncertainty-aware teaming: estimating and calibrating when a learned policy will succeed given human context, and using such estimates to decide

The Team

Our team in the Robotics division is developing pretrained generalist policies that can support a broad range of tasks, environments, and robotic systems. A central scientific challenge is determining how these broadly pretrained policies can be efficiently adapted to new target tasks while achieving the reliability, precision, and robustness required for real-world use.

Pretraining can provide a policy with broad behavioral capabilities, but those capabilities may not immediately translate into dependable performance in a specific deployment setting. Effective post-training methods are therefore essential for converting general capabilities into policies that can adapt quickly, learn from limited additional data or interaction, and perform consistently on demanding downstream tasks.

The Opportunity 

Our research interests include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, human-in-the-loop learning, simulation, world models, policy distillation, and large-scale robot learning. We aim to advance the scientific foundations of policy adaptation while developing methods that may ultimately be evaluated or deployed within internal research projects involving real-world industrial tasks.

Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: 
Offline-to-online reinforcement learning
DAgger, imitation learning, and human-in-the-loop policy improvement
Sim-to-real policy distillation and adaptation
Policy improvement, planning, or data generation using world models
Data-efficient adaptation to new tasks and environments

The Mission
We are building general-purpose robots that can perform a wide variety of dexterous, multi-step tasks in everyday environments. Our Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) are foundation models that generate robot actions from sensor data and natural-language requests. They are trained on a large curriculum of robot demonstrations, combined with internet-scale text, image, and video data and procedurally generated simulation data.
A growing focus of the team is world action models: models that learn to predict both how the world will change and which actions the robot should take. Because they capture the consequences of actions, these models can support planning over long horizons, recovery from errors, and anticipation of what nearby people are likely to do.
The Challenge
We envision robots that help with household chores and cooking, support older adults in living independently, and work side by side with people. These settings are messy and unstructured, and useful tasks often take minutes rather than seconds. A robot must chain many skills together, notice and recover from mistakes, and adapt to the people around it.
Our central question is what it will take for humanoids or other mobile manipulators to complete such long-horizon tasks reliably, safely, and naturally alongside people. We believe world action models, grounded in large-scale physical interaction data, are a key part of the answer for robot policy learning.
The Internship
We are seeking a research intern to adapt pre-trained world foundation models—through mid-training, fine-tuning, or post-training techniques—into world action models that serve as robot policies. These policies will be deployed on humanoid platforms or other mobile manipulators functioning within human-centered environments. Project focus areas can be customized based on your research interests, spanning model architecture design and training, long-horizon task execution, dynamic human-robot interaction, or real-world physical robot evaluation.
You will work closely with researchers and engineers on the team to turn ideas into working prototypes, run experiments in simulation and on real robots, and publish results at peer-reviewed venues. You should be comfortable working with large existing datasets as well as a growing corpus of robot and human-interaction data.
Areas of Focus
World action models for long-horizon tasks.
Human-robot interaction and collaboration.
Humanoid whole-body manipulation.
Cross-embodiment transfer

The Team/Project
TRI's Robotics Division develops technologies that enable robots to operate effectively in complex, real-world environments. The project explores how foundation-model agents can understand manipulation tasks, reason about physical environments, and orchestrate reusable robotic capabilities to accomplish diverse objectives. Our research combines vision-language models, robotic perception, motion planning, manipulation, and robot learning. We investigate these questions through hands-on experimentation on physical robotic platforms.
The Challenge
Recent advances in foundation models have significantly improved AI systems' ability to understand visual scenes, reason about tasks, and plan sequences of actions. However, translating these capabilities into reliable physical robot behavior remains challenging. Robots must reason about three-dimensional geometry, physical constraints, contact interactions, and failures during execution.
An important research question is how far foundation-model agents can go by leveraging existing robotic capabilities, and when specialized learned policies become necessary.
The Opportunity
We are seeking a Robotics Research Intern to investigate agentic approaches to robotic manipulation. You will work closely with researchers and engineers to develop systems that connect foundation-model reasoning with physical robot capabilities.
Depending on your background and research interests, your project may focus on spatial reasoning, robotic skill orchestration, execution monitoring, failure recovery, or systematic evaluation of agentic manipulation systems.
This internship offers an opportunity to tackle open research questions while gaining practical experience with cutting-edge AI models and real robotic systems. Your work will contribute to understanding how foundation-model agents can enable more generalizable and reliable robot autonomy.

Tyndall is Ireland’s leading research and innovation organisation, and it is the national focal point for excellence in deep-tech research, development and graduate training at the convergence of nanotechnology, microelectronics, photonics, electronics and AI. Tyndall is recognised as an international research leader in semiconductor, chip and digital technologies, particularly as applied to the fields of Information & Communications, Health & Life Sciences, Agritech & Food Security, Energy and Climate Mitigation, emerging fields such as quantum, and novel computing paradigms. The Institute’s key objective is to see frontier research activities having a significant impact on economic development and societal challenges in Ireland, Europe and beyond. Central to Tyndall’s mission is delivering economic impact through research excellence in partnership with industry and academia. With an annual turnover of more than €50m, the Institute has a community of over 600 researchers, engineers, support staff, postgraduate students, interns and industry researchers-in-residence. With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland. Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation. verkor-grenoble::94bab301-0d23-48a1-8d6d.desc:
As a Battery Pack Architect, you are responsible for defining the overall system architecture and ensuring the technical coherence and performance of the battery pack. You drive key design decisions by balancing electrochemical, electrical, thermal, mechanical, and safety constraints to deliver a solution that is safe, high-performing, manufacturable, and cost-effective.

verkor-grenoble::73d085ce-758d-4610-bb8b.title: Battery Testing Engineer
verkor-grenoble::73d085ce-758d-4610-bb8b.desc:
Verkor is a French industrial company aiming to pioneer low-carbon battery manufacturing in France. With the backing of prominent industrial companies such as Renault Group, Plastic Omnium and Schneider Electric, Verkor intends to electrify the future of European mobility.
 
With over 1100 experts from 53 different countries, our endeavor is to unite exceptional global talent to bring this ambitious and innovative project to life. Our strong and agile international team continues to grow and adapt to new challenges. Based in Grenoble and Dunkirk (France), we have started operations our Verkor Innovation Centre (R&D centre and 4.0 pilot line) which is now fully running and operational.
 
We now focus on enabling  the successful start of production of our Gigafactory in Dunkirk (France). With this facility, our ambition is to ramp-up mass production of low carbon lithium ion batteries to facilitate the decarbonization of European mobility.  
 


To elaborate and participate in the elaboration of tools and jigs to test variety of lithium ion cell R&D prototypes including coin cell, pouch cell and cylindrical cell : electrical and mechanical set-up
To perform test benches setup and wiring : upgrade, sensors adding, mechanical modification, measurement specifications
To specify the test benches, chambers, utilities in the scope of the testing center development with support from the validation team
To support the construction team on testing equipment's preparation and installation
To develop the testing equipment
To schedule tests according to tests standards and qualification plans and anticipate their preparation
To conduct and report internal tests in compliance with programs, procedures and safety rules
To perform cell testing and assist cell test fixtures definition : parametrization, measurement first analysis, conformity check, issues analysis and reporting
To specify the testing work-packages for tests outsourcing with the specification from validation team
To organize external tests and ensure their follow-up and exploitation
To work on the optimization of process parameters to improve performance, quality and yield
To perform the formalization and standardization of protocols and intellectual property via documentation generation/revision (work instructions, electronic notebook, …)
To provide a support in maintenance and troubleshooting of benches equipment
To participate on Verkor lab certification and accreditation readyness (IATF, ISO 17025,...)

verkor-grenoble::a92dbc4e-964e-435a-b488.title: Edge Engineer M/F
verkor-grenoble::a92dbc4e-964e-435a-b488.desc:
Verkor est une entreprise industrielle française dont l’ambition est d’être le pionnier de la fabrication de batteries à faible émission de carbone en France. Avec le soutien d’acteurs industriels de premier plan tels que le groupe Renault, Plastic Omnium et Schneider Electric, Verkor poursuit sa mission : accélérer l’électrification de la mobilité européenne.
 
Aujourd’hui, plus de 1 000 collaborateurs issus de 50 pays mettent en commun leurs talents, représentant plus de 1 200 ans d’expérience cumulée en matière de batteries, pour donner vie à ce projet ambitieux et innovant. Notre équipe internationale, solide et agile, continue de grandir et de s’adapter aux défis technologiques et industriels. 
 
Basés à Grenoble et à Dunkerque (France), nous disposons désormais d’un Verkor Innovation Centre opérationnel, regroupant notre centre de R&D et notre ligne pilote 4.0.La Gigafactory de Dunkerque, inaugurée le 11 décembre 2025, constitue aujourd’hui un pilier de notre montée en cadence. 
 
L'année 2026 est consacrée à accélérer sa production et au démarrage de nos premières lignes de production. En rejoignant Verkor, vous contribuerez activement à une aventure industrielle exceptionnelle, au cœur de la transition énergétique et de l’avenir de la mobilité européenne.

Verkor est une entreprise industrielle française dont l’ambition est d’être le pionnier de la fabrication de batteries à faible émission de carbone en France. Avec le soutien d’acteurs industriels de premier plan tels que le groupe Renault, Plastic Omnium et Schneider Electric, Verkor poursuit sa mission : accélérer l’électrification de la mobilité européenne.
 
Aujourd’hui, plus de 1 000 collaborateurs issus de 50 pays mettent en commun leurs talents, représentant plus de 1 200 ans d’expérience cumulée en matière de batteries, pour donner vie à ce projet ambitieux et innovant. Notre équipe internationale, solide et agile, continue de grandir et de s’adapter aux défis technologiques et industriels. 
 
Basés à Grenoble et à Dunkerque (France), nous disposons désormais d’un Verkor Innovation Centre opérationnel, regroupant notre centre de R&D et notre ligne pilote 4.0.La Gigafactory de Dunkerque, inaugurée le 11 décembre 2025, constitue aujourd’hui un pilier de notre montée en cadence. 
 
L'année 2026 est consacrée à accélérer sa production et au démarrage de nos premières lignes de production. En rejoignant Verkor, vous contribuerez activement à une aventure industrielle exceptionnelle, au cœur de la transition énergétique et de l’avenir de la mobilité européenne.

vtt-technical-research-centre-of-finland.title: Intelligent automation expert, Plastics Processing
vtt-technical-research-centre-of-finland.desc: Do you want to shape the future of plastics processing intelligent automation? Are you an expert in intelligent automation and data processing and ready to turn ideas into impact and grow with us? VTT might be just the place for you. VTT is one of the leading applied research organizations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning, and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2000 brilliant minds from 55+ different nationalities focus on creating impact through science-based innovation. Get to know us further by exploring VTT's tech & infra . We are now looking for Senior Scientist focusing on intelligent automation to join our materials processing and circular solutions team. In this role, you will strengthen our capabilities in process automation, data acquisition, and data-driven process control for plastics processing and recycling. You will work hands-on with pilot-scale equipment, particularly extrusion and plastics pre-treatment processes, developing solutions that connect process and sensor data with automation, control and online analytics. You will apply data-driven and machine-learning methods to process and sensor data, for example to derive online quality metrics and enable smarter process control. Your work will initially focus on extrusion-based process control and the automation and digitalization of plastics pre-treatment, including washing and sorting. You will also contribute to connecting our laboratory and pilot-scale equipment and their data to broader data architectures. Depending on your interests, there will be opportunities to develop new research directions beyond these initial applications. "We have a healthy work culture where you can be yourself, share your views, and improve things without fear of making mistakes - that’s what makes the work truly meaningful. " -Your new Team Leader Marjaana Mussalo- Our team is located in VTT’s Industrial Chemistry research area and focuses on the development of thermoplastic materials, their processing, and sensor-, spectroscopy- and software-enabled process control methods. Our target is to advance sustainable thermoplastic materials and products with high performance and increased circularity. We have unique pilot facilities for thermoplastic compounding, pre-industrial converting, and material characterization. In addition to these, we have unique pilot opportunities for identifying, sorting, washing and advanced mechanical recycling of plastic waste. The Material Processing and Circular Solutions team works in close collaboration with our customers and other research teams at VTT with business development and customer-oriented approach. The position is located in Tampere. zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1052189.title: (Senior) Data Engineer (f/m/d)
zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1052189.desc: ZEISS Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology​ ​ Enabler for smaller, more powerful, and more energy-efficient microchips​ ​ Working for tomorrow today. ​ Around 80 percent of all microchips worldwide are produced using ZEISS technologies. ZEISS is a technology leader in the field of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Your role: Conceptualization, implementation, and further development of data models that seamlessly link development, manufacturing, SAP, and supply-chain data Translating physical and process requirements into robust, traceable data models (OLAP/OLTP, Data Vault, dimensional modeling) Collaboration with process and domain experts to clarify definitions, thresholds, quality rules, and compliance requirements Design and implementation of data governance, quality checks, metadata management, and lineage tracking Implementation of production data pipelines (ETL/ELT) via Kafka Streams, dbt transformations, and on-prem (notably Trino) as well as cloud environments (notably Databricks) using CI/CD (Quality Gates, automated tests) Ensuring data consistency, visibility, and availability for analytics, AI/ML models, and simulations Development of performance and scaling strategies including monitoring, profiling, and performance tuning Mentoring less experienced Data Engineers, promoting best practices and code reviews Contributions to architecture decisions, security-by-design, and data privacy requirements Your profile: Strong data modeling expertise: 5–7 years of cross-domain data modeling experience (Data Vault, dimensional, logical/physical) — ideally in a complex manufacturing or high-tech environment Bridge between physics and data: Proven ability to collaborate with domain experts in manufacturing, development, or engineering and translate highly complex, physically grounded processes into robust data models Turning poor data quality into an strength: Experience in systematic profiling, assessment, and cleaning of heterogeneous, historically grown data sources — you see data chaos as a design challenge, not a hurdle Mastery of a hybrid tech stack: Hands-on experience with Trino (on-prem), dbt (transformation & documentation), Apache Kafka (streaming), and Databricks (Delta Lake, Spark); know the strengths and limits of each tool Seizing new technologies: Very good familiarity with state-of-the-art GenAI models and their reliable use to improve and accelerate daily work; also aware of their limits and safe-use requirements SAP and supply-chain data competence: Familiarity with SAP data structure

zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1052880.title: Leitung Montage und Justage von Lithographieoptiken (m/w/x)
zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1052880.desc: Sich heute mit ZEISS den Herausforderungen von morgen stellen. Als Teil der Sparte Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology tragen wir mit unseren hochpräzisen DUV-Lithographieoptiken maßgeblich dazu bei, die nächste Generation von Mikrochips zu ermöglichen. Am Standort Wetzlar entsteht mit dem neuen Werksteil im Dillfeld eine hochmoderne Fab für die Fertigung von Lithographieoptiken. Als Erweiterung unseres bestehenden Werks in der Gloelstraße wurde im Dillfeld ein neues Werk mit einem Investitionsvolumen im höheren dreistelligen Millionenbereich errichtet. Aktuell werden neue Anlagen eingebracht, qualifiziert und in den Produktionsverbund integriert; in den kommenden Monaten wird die Produktion weiter hochgefahren. Damit übernimmt Wetzlar eine zentrale Rolle im weiteren Ausbau der DUV-Fertigung – von der Optikfertigung über Montage und Justage bis hin zu einer zunehmend automatisierten, digital unterstützten und skalierbaren Wertschöpfung. In dieser Schlüsselrolle übernehmen Sie die Gesamtverantwortung für eine Reinraum-Montage und Justage hochpräziser Lithographieoptiken in beiden Werksteilen. Sie prägen den weiteren Aufbau des neuen Werksteils Dillfeld, skalieren leistungsfähige Strukturen und führen eine erfahrene Organisation sicher durch ambitionierte Wachstums- und Ramp-up-Phasen. Gesucht wird eine Führungspersönlichkeit, die technologische Exzellenz, operative Stärke und nachweisliche Umsetzungserfolge verbindet – und ein Umfeld schafft, in dem Führungskräfte, Teams, Prozesse und Technologie nachhaltig wirksam werden. Ihre Rolle Fachliche und disziplinarische Führung eines Fertigungssegments mit 5 Teams und ca. 100 Mitarbeitenden. Gesamtverantwortung für Sicherheit, Qualität, Lieferfähigkeit, Produktivität, Kosten sowie die stabile Erreichung ambitionierter Wachstums- und Ramp-up-Ziele. Aufbau, Steuerung und Weiterentwicklung der Montage und Justage im neuen Werksteil Dillfeld als integraler Teil der werksübergreifenden Fertigung in Wetzlar. Gestaltung einer skalierbaren, zukunftsorientierten Produktion mit modernen Fertigungs-, Automatisierungs- und Digitalisierungslösungen. Optimierung von Wertströmen, Kapazitäten, Ressourcen, Schichtmodellen und Materialflüssen im Produktionsnetzwerk der Carl Zeiss SMT. Übersetzung von Unternehmens- und Standortzielen in klare KPIs, Prioritäten und operative Entscheidungen für Ihre Teams. Weiterentwicklung von Führungskräften, Teams und Organisation mit Fokus auf Eigenverantwortung, Leistungsbereitschaft und kontinuierliche Verbesserung. Souveräner Umgang mit Konflikten, Veränderungen und Zielkonflikten sowie enge Zusammenarbeit mit Standortleitung, Engineering, Qualität, Supply Chain, HR und angrenzenden Fertigungssegmenten. Ihr Profil Sehr gut abgeschlossenes Studium in Ingenieurwissenschaften, Produktionstechnik, Maschinenbau, Physik, Optik oder vergleichbar; Promotion von Vorteil. Good knowledge in at least several of the following areas: mechanics and precision mechanics, pneumatics and possibly hydraulics, assembly and adjustment of mechanical subsystems, technical drawings and bill of materials, systematic fault analysis. zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1053823.title: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (m/w/x) für optische Messtechnik in der Halbleiterfertigung
zeiss-smt-oberkochen::JR_1053823.desc: Enabler für kleinere, leistungsfähigere und energieeffizientere Mikrochips - Arbeiten, wo das Morgen entsteht. Rund 80 Prozent aller Mikrochips weltweit werden mit ZEISS Technologien gefertigt. Als Herzstück eines jeden elektronisch gesteuerten Systems sind sie aus unserem Alltag nicht mehr wegzudenken – egal ob im Smartphone, im Smart Home oder in Smart Factories. ZEISS ist Technologieführer im Bereich Halbleiterfertigungs-Equipment. Mit hochpräzisen Lithographie-Optiken, Photomasken-Systemen und Lösungen für die Prozesskontrolle ermöglicht ZEISS die Herstellung von immer kleineren, leistungsfähigeren und energieeffizienteren Mikrochips – und prägt so mit seinen Innovationen das Zeitalter der Mikro- und Nanoelektronik entscheidend mit. Ihre Rolle Sie spezifizieren komplexe Messsysteme ganzheitlich und leiten Anforderungen an Subsysteme ab. Sie entwickeln, implementieren und validieren Mess-, Auswerte- und Simulationsalgorithmen, die produktionstauglich sind. Sie führen experimentelle und theoretische Messgenauigkeitsanalysen optischer Messsysteme durch. Sie entwickeln Baugruppen für interferometrische Messmaschinen in Zusammenarbeit mit internen und externen Partnern und implementieren diese in Abstimmung mit dem Betreiber. Sie betreuen komplexe Messmaschinen im Fertigungsumfeld; ggf. Fehler suchen, Gegenmaßnahmen ableiten und deren Umsetzung sicherstellen. Sie entwickelten gezielte Maschinenverbesserungen und führen diese zur Serientauglichkeit. Sie leiten eigenverantwortlich Teil-Projekte im Bereich Sondermaschinenbau mit Messtechnik-Schwerpunkt.
